articles.title: Pikmin 4 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Pikmin 4 at IGN: walkthroughs, items, maps, video tips, and strategies
articles.body:
IGN's Pikmin 4 guide features a 100% Walkthrough , including the All Treasure Locations , Flarlic Locations , and Side Missions , complete with maps and handy checklists to make sure you've gotten them all. Pikmin 4 was released for the Nintendo Switch on July 21, 2023.

For the 2026 Switch 2 release, Pikmin 4 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy, we also added a Dandori Academy Tips page.

Playing Pikmin for the first time or just want to know what's new in Pikmin 4? Our Beginner's Guide is designed to cover all the basics and features.

Beginner's Guide - Basics and Features - check out the story overview, currencies, collectibles, and game modes you can expect to find

All Pikmin Types - get to know each of the main Pikmin types you'll encounter throughout the game

Oatchi Guide - Skills, Upgrades, and Tips - teach this dog some new tricks with our guide to skills and upgrades for Oatchi

Walkthrough - Every boss fight, every Treasure, and every little Pikmin you can add to your team. This is the best way to play Pikmin 4.

Collectibles - Treasures, Flarlics, and Onion Locations

Flarlic Locations - Flarlics can be used to increase the amount of Pikmin you can have outside your onion.

Onion Locations - Onions come in every color to correspond with each Pikmin type. Collect them all to continue blooming Pikmin as often as you like.

While you're rounding up the Rescue Corps , there are Civilian Castaways you'll need to find too. As they join the Rescue Command Post , you'll need to satisfy their demands to get great rewards.

Missing Crewmates and Civilian Castaway Locations - find them all with handy maps and explanations of their locations

Side Missions - tackle all the side missions to earn Raw Material and unique items

Dandori Battles - ready to go head-to-head? Find out where you can battle and prove your Dandori skills

Dandori Challenges - keep your Dandori skills sharp in these timed challenges

Up Next: Beginner's Guide - Basics and Features

articles.title: Annual Events and Celebrations Guide - Hello Kitty Island Adventure Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Throughout the year, experience a wide range of Annual Events that celebrate friendship, the seasons, the art of expression, and so much more in Hello Kitty
articles.body:
Throughout the year, experience a wide range of Annual Events that celebrate friendship, the seasons, the art of expression, and so much more in Hello Kitty Island Adventure . These events will showcase exclusive furniture and outfits that you can only obtain when the event is live, daily rewards for checking in, and adorable scenes featuring you and your friends.

Hello Kitty Island Adventure will almost always feature a center-focused event that’ll last around a month and smaller events that run about a week in between these main events. Some events will be the primary focus, rewarding you in only one Event Currency for doing Daily Quests, even when another event could start during the same duration. Visit the pages below to see which events are active, how long they last, and what exclusive items you can get during those events.

Race into the new Interlude of Dreams by pairing up with your Hello Kitty pals for a sports car competition! This year, Interlude of Dreams introduces a brand new mini-game, Formula Fun, where you and five other characters from the island compete on a race track for 1st place.

articles.title: I didn’t expect to love Dyson’s PencilVac Fluffycones – but I did
articles.summary: Dyson’s new super-slim, super-light stick vacuum is designed to be seen, not heard.
articles.body: As The Verge’s resident robot vacuum reviewer, I don’t have a lot of time (or space) in my life for stick vacs, and frankly, the ones I have used have largely disappointed me. Top-heavy, bulky, always getting clogged or running out of battery — they’re so… manual. But then I met PencilVac Fluffycones, Dyson’s new $599 cordless stick vacuum, and it was love at first lift. The name PencilVac Fluffycones perfectly describes this delightfully overengineered broom. If more vacuums had such whimsical names, my life would be much fuller. It’s very thin and light, like a pencil, and it has fluffy, cone-shaped rollers that glide across floors as if they’re flying. While I do not recommend buying this as a tool to clean your entire home (it doesn’t clean carpets!), with its slim design and easy maneuverability, I’ve found it to be a great complement to a robot vacuum. The robot can do the hard work of vacuuming and mopping your floors, and this lightweight machine, which sits prettily in a magnetic charging dock, can be on hand for touch-ups and when it’s time to tackle stairs and baseboards. [Product: PencilVac Fluffycones | Touted by Dyson as “the world’s slimmest vacuum cleaner,” the PencilVac fits all its components into its 1.5-inch-diameter handle, which runs the length of the vacuum. Packed in here are the electronics, the battery, the dustbin, and a tiny 28mm-diameter motor that spins at 140,000 RPM to generate 55 air watts of suction. This is the same motor as in Dyson’s Supersonic R hair dryer, and the handle is the same width around, so you’re basically using a reverse hair dryer to clean your floors. Impressively, the PencilVac weighs less than four pounds and, combined with its maneuverability enabled by four caster rollers that allow it to pivot in multiple directions, it’s as easy to handle as a broom or Swiffer. Even my husband, who just had major shoulder surgery, was able to use it to clean the kitchen floor with no issues. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: The PencilVac’s other unique selling point is its fluffycones — four fluffy, cone-shaped roller bars in the vacuum’s head. The idea is that long hair should move down the four cones and out from the edge of the vacuum, then be sucked up with a swipe. In practice, this worked fairly well, unless the aforementioned bundle of hair got too thick — in which case, it couldn’t always suck it up. While the PencilVac looks and moves like a broom, it also kind of vacuums like one. Its suction power is half that of Dyson’s lowest-end cordless stick vacuum, the V8. It does great on dust, small tufts of hair, and lightweight debris like Cheerios and dried oatmeal. But give it anything thicker to tackle, and you’ll be frustrated. [Image: [Image: This is why it works well as an add-on to a robot vacuum that regularly sweeps and mops your floors. Judging by Dyson’s press images, it’s also being marketed as a stylish option for those who live in immaculate apartments that are magically mostly spotless. Unless you live in one of those apartments, I don’t see the PencilVac working as a primary vacuum for cleaning your house, especially if you have any carpets or rugs. But for quick touch-ups and getting dust bunnies off stairs — two areas robot vacuums don’t really do (one not easily, and the other not at all … yet) — it’s a great, albeit expensive, solution. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: Less cumbersome than any stick vac I’ve used, it is super easy to use on stairs, and it was simple to find a space for its small, slim dock in a kitchen or bathroom, areas where you might want a high-powered broom on hand. [Image: The PencilVac’s magnetic charging stand is small, unobtrusive, and easy to use. It’s more maneuverable than a stick vac, pivoting smoothly to go around furniture legs and lying completely flat to get under sofas and beds. For deeper cleaning, the PencilVac’s included crevice tool/dusting attachment did a good job on baseboards and windowsills, and could reach up to lights and cobwebby corners. It also easily got into spaces robot vacuums can’t — like the gap behind the TV console. I’ve only been using it for a couple of days, but I quickly got used to the lack of a handle. It really is just like using a broom. The biggest problem is suction; it’s not a powerful vacuum, especially compared to Dyson’s stick vacs. It struggles with larger clumps of dirt and anything bigger than a fluffy dust bunny. As mentioned, it just flat-out doesn’t work on carpet. It also only runs for 30 minutes on low and around 20 minutes on medium, which I found myself using most often. (There is a boost mode for some extra power.) All of which makes it great for a quick touch-up, but not for a whole-house clean. One other thing to note: this is Dyson’s first stick vacuum to connect to the My Dyson app. This isn’t a plus, at least not yet. Functionally, it’s limited to software updates and filter-cleaning alerts. It also uses Bluetooth, so you have to be near the vacuum to update it, and the app kept insisting that I give it permanent access to my location for no clear reason. [Image: The PencilVac is an excellent lightweight machine for lightweight tasks. If you don’t expect more from it, you’ll be very happy. Between the limited suction, short runtime, and inability to handle carpet, the PencilVac Fluffycones isn’t even pretending to be a whole-home cleaner. If you’re looking for a proper house cleaner in this price range, Dyson’s V8 Absolute is a better choice. It’s under six pounds and has twice the suction. While slightly less maneuverable, it will pick up all the dirt and clean your carpets, baseboards, and everything else. But is it as fun as the PencilVac? Not even close. The PencilVac is Dyson at its best: a wildly overengineered device that’s delightful to use, entirely unnecessary, but something you’re probably going to really want anyway. Photos by Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge

articles.title: Missing in the Desert - Gerudo Fortress Walkthrough - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Welcome to IGN's Guide to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. After 28 years, Ocarina of Time has been fully remade, and while much of it remains
articles.body:
Welcome to IGN's Guide to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. After 28 years, Ocarina of Time has been fully remade, and while much of it remains the same, there's plenty of new differences to be found while exploring Hyrule. Only one temple remains to be found, located far off beyond the sands of the Gerudo Desert. To get there, Link will need to infiltrate the Gerudo Fortress to rescue imprisoned carpenters.

Now that the Shadow Temple has been cleansed, there's only one area left to explore that was inaccessible when Link was a child. The followers of Ganondorf, known as the Gerudo, are a secretive clan of female warriors who guarded entrance to the vast desert where a temple is rumored to be hidden. Getting there will be quite the challenge, as Hylians aren't welcome in Gerudo territory.

You'll find the entrance to the fortress beyond Gerudo Valley to the west, a large arid region with a huge waterfall and river separating Hyrule Field from the desert compound. Though the place was initially locked when visiting in the past, you'll find that the bridge across the valley has now been completely destroyed. Funny enough, this actually makes it more accessible than ever.

There are two ways across the canyon -- you can either uses your new Longshot on the wooden panel above the broken bridge to zip across, or if you want to be more stylish, guide Epona across the first narrow bridge and then race forward to have her perform a mighty leap taking you across the gap!

Once on the other side, you'll find a worker's tent that is now mostly abandoned, save for a Running Man you probably met as a child in Hyrule Field and gave the Bunny Hood to. He's still looking for the spirit of the wilds, but is now trapped on this side of the ravine. Once the bridge is repaired, he'll be happy to challenge you to a race!

Nearby, the Master Craftsman from Kakariko can be found. His apprentice carpenters who helped build the village came to Gerudo Valley looking for employment from the Gerudo, but as they don't take kindly to visitors, they all got thrown in jail. While the Master Craftsman knows nothing about sages or temples, he'll reckon rescuing his men may help you out if they overheard anything.

Be sure to look around, and you'll find a few points of interest. A large selection of grey rocks to the side can be obliterated with your Megaton Hammer to reveal a Treasure Chest with a Red Rupee.

Over by the other side of the tent, there's a grotto entrance you can open by playing the Song of Storms, and inside you'll find one chest, and another that's invisible that holds another Red Rupee.

While you're in this area, be sure to turn day to night, as there are two Gold Skulltulas lurking around nearby. One can be found at the back of the worker's tent, on a wall carving.

Another Gold Skulltula can be found nearby. Head over to the section where all the grey rocks you smashed were, and look up at the natural rock arch. Up above along the rocks where the pillar is, you'll find the Gold Skulltula.

Finishing the Trading Quest - Biggoron Sword

Before you head off to rescue the carpenters, do you remember helping out the Craftsman's son in the Lost Woods? When he vanished, a Kokiri girl gave you a Poacher's Saw that belong to him, and you can now return it to the Master Craftsman. As thanks, he'll give you a Broken Goron Sword he's been meaning to repair, and will tell you that a giant Goron on top of Death Mountain can repair it!

Take a detour by warping to Death Mountain Crater and heading out onto the summit. You can speak to Biggoron as he's known, who is furiously rubbing at his eyes now. He'll still recognize his handiwork, but can't do any repairs while his eyes are full of Death Mountain ash.

If you want to get that sword repaired, you'll need to go about finding some eyedrops for the big guy. He'll give you a Prescription that can be filled by King Zora himself, who seems to have the remedy for such a problem.

Head back to Zora Domain and speak to King Zora and explain the problem. Unfortunately, King Zora doesn't have the eye drops... but he does have the key ingredient needed to make them, and the scientist working out of the Lake Hylia Laboratory has the tools to finish the job!

When you're ready, King Zora will give you the Eyeball Frog to take to the scientist, but warn you that like the Odd Mushroom, you'll only have a limited time to perform the trade before it spoils. This gives you just 2 Minutes and 30 Seconds to get to Lake Hylia!

You can't simply warp to Water Temple with the Seranade of Water, unfortunately. If you hadn't finished the Water Temple, you'd have to race all the way down Zora River and zoom across the field on Epona to barely make it, but since the waters have unfrozen, you can still use a massive shortcut to complete this task in seconds.

Just dive into the waters below the Audience Chamber and go through the tunnel to be transported to the lake. Swim to the shore, and sprint on over to the lab. At first, the scientist will want to eat the eyeballs, but when you give him the real reason, he'll begrudgingly make you some Specialty Eye Drops. Like the ingredient you raced over with, the drops will also expire relatively quickly, meaning you'll have one last mad dash to make to get back to Biggoron in time: Just 3 Minutes and 30 Seconds!

Since you can't warp to the Fire Temple, there are two ways to complete this task. The most straightforward one is to race Epona across Hyrule Field, sprint through Kakariko Village and up the Death Mountain Trail to the summit.

However, if you want to get stylish, there's a faster path: Dive back into Lake Hylia and use the shortcut to get whisked away to Zora Domain (assuming you cleared the Water Temple).

Hop out of the water and exit onto the falls above Zora River, and then dive into the shortcut nearby to transport yourself into the Lost Woods.

Once in the woods, sprint straight after exiting the water into the next area, where you can make an immediate right into the stone archway to transport yourself into Goron City.

Once in the city, hop down to the lowest level, and race out through Darunia's Chambers into Death Mountain Crater. From here, sprint up the south side, across the small gap and up the wall to reach the exit onto the summit!

However you get to the top, show the eyedrops to Biggoron, who will carefully apply them. When he's done, he'll immediately get to work on your new sword! This will take several days however, so he'll give you the Biggoron Receipt.

You can either go back to your main questing -- or if you're the impatient type, you can simple play the Sun's Song around 6-8 times to speed up the time it takes Biggoron to ply his trade. Once you notice he's stopped hammering, present your claim, and he'll be ready to give you his masterwork - the Biggoron Sword!

Like the Giant's Knife (which he'll swap out for you if you still have one), it deals incredible damage with a huge reach, but have a very slow wind-up, and you won't be able to block with it held at the ready. This officially ends the long trading quest, and you'll have a great new prize to remember it by!

Head up the path from the worker's tent to begin your rescue operation, but don't expect a warm welcome. In fact, to the patrolling Gerudo guards around the fortress, you're a primary target to capture on sight! Much like the guards of Hyrule Castle, if any of them happen to catch you in their line of sight, you'll be caught and unable to fight back.

However, this is actually to your advantage, as a frontal approach isn't necessarily the best one. Once caught, you'll be thrown into a prison cell with a very tall celing, which features an open skylight with a mesh ceiling your Longshot can reach!

From this balcony, you'll have a great vantage point to look over the fortress, which features multiple entrances and twisting paths between them. There's no single set path you're required to take, but we'll go with what's closest and easiest.

From the top of the jail, look down to spot a door and barred windows below you on the ground floor. There's one guard over by the gate to the desert, and two other further away that can't detect you from this distance when you drop down.

If you walk over to the barred windows, you'll spot the first of four imprisoned carpenters, Shiro, who will motion you toward the nearby door.

Enter the holding cell area and speak to Shiro behind bars, and he'll mention you need to be careful as there's probably a guard nearby. Lo' and behold, a Gerudo Thief will catch you in the act, and draw you into combat to try and knock you out.

Unlike the guards outside, you're not automatically busted, and will need to fight the Gerudo Thief off. She wields twin blades with deft precision, and can move with incredibly agility to perform a variety of quick and powerful swings.

Her attack usually starts by darting forward with a quick jump attack with good amount of reach for a vertical swing, and you'll want to dodge to the side or block the incoming strike. This will soon be followed up by her raising her blades and then leaping forward again in an uppercut slice. Once again, it's got a great deal of range and power, and simply backpedaling or dodging backward won't be enough, so strafe to the side. The attack has a long recovery period, giving you the chance to deal some damage of your own!

What you really need to be careful of is the Gerudo Thief's signature "Blade Storm". This always starts with her crouching down and leaning back, while holding her blades out wide. After a momentary pause, she'll leap forward in a spinning slice attack with a wild amount of range as she moves far and sweeps the area around her at the same time. If you get hit by any part of this attack, Link will be KO'd instantly, and you'll get tossed back into jail!

Even if you have the Biggoron Sword, play this fight safe and strategic, strafing your opponent at a distance to wait for the right moment to close in. Her attacks leave her wide open after the fact, but if you're too close when she prepares her Blade Storm, you'll need to sprint backward to avoid getting caught.

After taking enough damage, the Gerudo Thief will flee, giving you a Small Key to unlock the cell door. One craftsman has now been rescued, but you still have three more to find. He won't have any useful info on the temple, but suggests you find his friends.

Leave the cell block by heading south, and you'll come outside to an enclosed area in front of a large door, and thankfully a few stone walls protect you from being spotted by the guards out front.

Nearby, a voice will ring out, and you can inspect a grate on the floor to find your next imprisoned carpenter. He appears to be underground, so you'll need to find a way to head downstairs.

If you try going through the door to the east, you'll find stairs leading up to a patrolling Gerudo guard instead. You can try and slip past to the left to find a dead end with a Grotto entrance. It's a dark cave full of enemies guarding a Treasure Chest with a Red Rupee inside.

However, trying to slip past the patrolling guard to the south leads to a large communal room with two more guards that will spot you, so this isn't the route you want to take.

Instead, from the outdoor area, carefully look around the two low broken walls. A Gerudo guard stands at attention on the other side, looking out west, while another guard to the southwest patrols back and forth in this area. Just to the left of the stationary guard is a stairway down to the basement where the next carpenter is.

If you're slow and careful, you can slip past the stationary guard, and wait for the patrolling guard nearby to turn her back before moving over to the stairs, but if you want to play it safe, hit the stationary guard from behind with your Longshot, and it will stun her for a long moment, letting you slip past (Just don't let the other guard catch you in the act!).

Head through the door to the basement and drop down to the next cell block room. It's here you'll find Ichiro, the second carpenter in need of a rescue.

Just like before, the Gerudo Thief will appear to tangle with you again. She's got all the same moves as before, so fight defensively and dodge that Blade Storm until she gives up and retreats, leaving behind another Small Key. Rescue the carpenter, who has no useful information to give, and then depart.

There's a few ways to reach the next imprisoned carpenter. That indoor path the guard patrolled that you passed by earlier has a stairway leading up to the rooftops you could take to reach the third floor.

You can also simply head north from where you unlocked Ichiro's cell to find a long winding stairway leading up to the north side of the fortress rooftops. This large landing area has a solitary guard watching over the western edge that won't turn around, so instead keep heading south to find a ladder up to the third floor, and you'll find a doorway leading into the next cell block.

In here, you'll find Saburo, the third carpenter who's been imprisoned. Like all before him, speaking to him will trigger the Gerudo Thief to ambush you once more. By now you should know the drill -- be evasive, wait for openings, and avoid the Bladestorm.

Defeat her a third time to earn the next Small Key, and open up the cell to rescue Saburo. Sadly, he has no new information to give, but you've only got one left to free!

Like the craftsman you just rescued, getting to the final prisoner has multiple paths. From Saburo, the shortest path is heading back out onto the third floor balcony looking north, and enter the door on the right. This will put you back in the large room with two guards you couldn't enter from the floor below. Up here on a high walkway however, you can zip right past them by using the Longshot on the far doorway.

This leads up to a high rooftop, allowing you to drop down to a ledge to the north with another door.

Before entering the doorway on the ledge between the third and fourth floor, turn around to the south to find a low roof ledge you can climb. This path winds around the south side of the fortress all the way to a crumbled corner. Climb up the slope and onto the top rooftop and double back the way you came until you're above the doorway on the ledge.

On the far side, you can spot a gust of straw, and play the Scarecrow's Song to reveal Pierre. Zip across, and check this part of the roof for a large Treasure Chest holding a Piece of Heart!

When you to to drop back down below where you summoned Pierre to the doorway on the rooftop ledge, be sure to look up at the opposite wall when night has fallen. It's here you'll find one of two Gold Skulltulas in the Fortress (you can always come back for it when you're able to explore the place more freely).

Entering this new corridor takes you in a long path around the northeast corner of the fortress. Move slowly, as there's another guard who patrols the eastern corridor, and you'll need to wait for them to move north before slipping past to the cell block.

Alternatively, if you do get captured and thrown back in jail, there's a shorter path to the fourth cell block (though you don't pass by the Heart Piece and Spider). From the top of the jail, leap to the east to a high rooftop ledge with a doorway. In here, you'll be above a massive war room with patrolling guards and a large table, with two large chandeliers hanging overhead. To bypass them, use your Longshot on the wooden beams holding the chandeliers up, and jump between them to the northern end of the room to reach the cell block.

In here, you'll find Jiro, the last of the carpenters in need of a rescue. This also means you'll have to duke it out with the Gerudo Thief one last time, but by now you should be an expert on taking her down without getting hit too much in return.

Once defeated, you'll gain the last Small Key needed, and send Jiro on his way back to the worker camp with the rest of the carpenters! Sadly, none of them seem to know anything about a temple or sage in this area.

This time, as you move to leave, you'll be intercepted by the Gerudo Captain of the fortress. She can see you're quite talented fighter, and heard you asking about the temple. She just happens to know where the Spirit Temple is, but has a proposition: Find out what became of the Gerudo leader, Nabooru, who departed across the desert to reach the temple, and they'll allow you to cross the desert after her.

To ensure you aren't hassled anymore by the guards, you'll also be given a special Gerudo Pass so that all the Gerudo around the fortress no longer consider you hostile!

That said, do mind your manners. If they were to, say, catch you standing on top of Ganondorf's War Table, they might just throw you back in jail for being a jerk!

Now that you have the run of the place, there's a few extra things you can check out:

From Ganondorf's War Table, head east back to the jail you were tossed in so regularly. Just outside the cell is a ladder leading to a high alcove, and you can roll into a crate here to find a Purple Rupee!

There's a large road leading to the southeast, and it passes by a large imposing gate. The Gerudo outside will inform you that it's the Gerudo Training Grounds - a test of skill involving several challenging rooms, all hiding keys that you'll need to use to progress toward a prize at the center of the grounds: The Ice Arrows! You can try it out now and actually win if you actually unlock the right doors, but one area will be impassible with your current equipment, so we'll cover it after the Spirit Temple.

Just past the Training Grounds, you can find the large horseback archery range. It's here you can take the ultimate archery skill test and try your hand at scoring big points by hitting every target you can -- including a line of pots, and several large targets. The more bullseyes you hit, the better your score!

If you earn at least 750 points, you can gain a new Heart Piece, and if you manage to best a score of 1,400, you'll earn the Biggest Quiver, allowing you to hold a maximum of 50 Arrows!

Be sure to return to the Horseback Archery Course when night has fallen. Take Epona and ride to the northern side, and then look up at the large towering target. Around the back of the target on its bullseye is a Gold Skulltula you can take down and grab its token with the Longshot!

When you're ready to depart, head to the large gate in the northwest. There's a lookout up top who wonders if Nabooru ever met a guide to get her across the desert, and it sounds like quite the trip. The guard below will warn you that it's very easy to get lost or stuck in quicksand, but you can find your way as as long as you follow the flagposts and have the "eyes of truth".

Entering the desert, you'll find there's no map to guide you, and a blinding sandstorm makes visibility incredibly poor, regardless of whether it's day or night!

Blocking the way forward, you'll find a large ravine of shifting sands. If you try to step into it, you'll quickly be sucked down into quicksand and have to start over again. Luckily, with your Longshot, you'll have just enough range to stand on the edge of the quicksand and fire away at a wood panel between two large posts on the opposite side.

Once you reach the other side of the quicksand, your next task is to get through the raging sandstorm using only a scattered set of flagposts as your guide. With visibility tough, you'll want to approach each one slowly, then pan around to spot the next flag billowing through the storm and walk a straight line to the next.

You'll start by heading west, before taking a curve to the north up a sand dune, and heading a little to the northeast over a few more dunes before turning west along a slope, and then north between two poles that crest a large dune.

A large structure will appear as you head down the other side of the large sand dune, flanked by flagpoles. In the center, you'll find a plaque that reads "Those with eyes of truth shall be guided to the Spirit Temple by a welcoming specter."

Before you take the next leg of your journey, be sure to check out the bottom of the structure for a hidden resting spot below ground. There's a lone torch and two extra braziers, and if you light all three, a small Treasure Chest will appear holding a Business Scrub Seed.

While down in the underground resting chamber below the sands and main structure, be sure to turn day to night with the Sun's Song. Against the far wall behind where the chest will appear, a Gold Skulltula will also appear to take down.

When standing before the plaque, don your Lenses of Truth, and you'll behold your Phantom Guide. This clever Poe will see you across to the far side of the desert, but you'll need to be quick!

The Phantom Guide will take a brisk pace through the desert, winding back and forth and changing directions on a whim. You'll want to sprint quickly to keep pace but be ready to alter your movements at a moment's notice. To make matters worse, enemies called Leevers will burrow out of the sand to careen into you. Luckily, their charging path is hard for them to change, so dodge around them and don't bother fighting back so you can focus on crossing the desert.

Once you hit the far eastern side, you'll find the goal posts that mark the entrance to an oasis, and the guide will depart. Don't worry, we'll find our own way back.

The majestic colossus (that's also somehow evil) makes for an impressive sight as the sculpture built into the side of a large rocky outcropping dominated the landscape of this mostly barren area.

You'll be constantly beset by Leevers when here, but as they keep appearing no matter how many you kill, it's best to avoid them or stick to higher ground off the sand when possible.

Note there's a nice looking spot to the south surrounded by palm trees, but seems to be missing something. If you play the Song of Storms, you'll bring water to the oasis, and spawn in a Fairy Fountain to help replenish your hearts!

Speaking of fairies, be sure to travel along the northern edge of this area, and you can find a large cracked wall between some palm trees. Blast it open, and you'll find an entrance to another Great Fairy Fountain! Like the rest, you'll need to make an offering if you want the Fairy's power, and this one costs a whopping 300 Rupees!

If you accept to this request, the Great Fairy of Magic will appear before you, and grant you a new special power: Nayru's Love. This exceptional spell grants you a protective barrier to make you effectively invulnerable for a short duration, but is also a massive drain on your magic meter!

While you're out exploring the desert here, you can also check a rocky area in the far northwest. A large group of Guay swoop around this spot with a leader (colored green) that you can take out to disperse the rest. If you wait until nightfall, a Gold Skulltula appears on the northern rocks in this area as well!

As you approach the large stone arch in front of the colossus, Sheik will appear. The Sheikah warrior has one last melody to teach you:

articles.title: Lanterns Season 1 Is Up for Preorder on 4K UHD and Blu-ray
articles.body:
The first season of the DC show Lanterns, which recently ended on HBO, is now available to preorder on 4K UHD and Blu-ray. The price of the collection currently varies widely at retailers, but Amazon has it for the lowest prices; it costs $39.98 on 4K or $29.95 on Blu-ray . It's also available on DVD elsewhere, if you want it. Whichever format you choose, it's set to release on February 9. Read on to see what this show is and where else it’s available.

Lanterns - The Complete First Season (4K UHD)

Lanterns is an HBO show based on the DC comic Green Lantern. It stars Kyle Chandler as Hal Jordan, along with Aaron Pierre, Nathan Fillion, and others. It was created by Chris Mundy, Damon Lindelof, and Tom King, and it often downplays its superhero origins to focus on a gritty, small-town murder mystery. That said, there are plenty of twists and turns, and it ends up having larger implications for the greater DC universe.

This collection includes all eight hour-long episodes of the first season of the show, spread across three discs. It also includes “Inside the Episode” featurettes, as well as some as-yet-unannounced “Exclusive-to-home-entertainment” special features.

From IGN’s spoiler-free Lanterns premier review , critic Jesse Schedeen wrote, “With the DCU suddenly on shaky ground following the disastrous reception to Supergirl, it’s reassuring to see Lanterns get off to such a strong start. It proves that there’s indeed room for superhero stories in this cinematic universe that aren’t all cut from the James Gunn cloth. While the central murder mystery in Episode 1 is more serviceable than actively intriguing, the characters and their uneasy dynamics more than justify giving the show a watch. Chandler’s Hal Jordan and Pierre’s John Stewart make for a mighty but very dysfunctional Dynamic Duo, and the prospect of spending seven more hours with them is exciting indeed.”

The first episode only scratches the surface of what is to come in this season of television. You can check out the full reviews for all episodes of Lanterns here .

While James Gunn and Peter Safran’s recent departure from their positions as co-CEOs of DC Studios may call the future of Lanterns into question, this release is labeled “The Complete First Season,” which seems to suggest a second season was at least being planned when this first season was being packaged for release. To date, however, Lanterns has not been officially renewed for a second season.

Chris Reed is a senior commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's LEGO coverage and maintains the upcoming release dates articles for video games , LEGO sets , and 4K Blu-rays . You can follow him on Bluesky .

articles.title: VisionQuest Ending Explained: Why the Series Is Surprisingly Important to Avengers - Doomsday
articles.summary: We break down the surprising ending to VisionQuest and why the series has unexpectedly become a major building block to Avengers: Doomsday.
articles.body:
If you just want to know whether VisionQuest has a post-credits scene, the answer is yes. The final episode features both a mid-credits scene and a post-credits scene.

Full spoilers for VisionQuest Episode 8 ahead!

VisionQuest has wrapped its eight-episode run on Disney+, marking the end of the final MCU project leading into Avengers: Doomsday. And as it happens, the series proves more relevant to Doomsday than we would have expected. There’s a post-credits scene that directly leads into Marvel’s big Avengers reunion.

So how does the series set up Doomsday and the unexpected return of a major MCU player? And where does the show leave Paul Bettany’s Vision and James Spader’s Ultron? Let’s break down the key developments in the series finale.

All season long, Vision and his estranged son, Tommy (Ruaridh Mollica) have worked to stay one step ahead of “The Client,” the shadowy villain who hired Paladin (Todd Stashwick) and has been manipulating Jocasta (T’Nia Miller). All the evidence pointed to The Client being either original A.I. inventor Phineas Horton or his signature creation J.I.M. (both of whom are also played by Bettany in Episode 7). But the finale throws viewers for a loop by revealing that The Client is actually Phineas’ grandson, Virgil (Spader), the human model for Ultron.

As we learn in the finale, Virgil despises the legacy of failure his grandfather left behind. His goal is to wipe Vision’s memory banks and implant his consciousness into the synthezoid’s body, thereby allowing him to live forever as a new breed of human/android hybrid. Virgil is foiled, but not before he shoots and mortally wounds Jocasta. Needless to say, Ultron is not amused, and he promptly squeezes his “father” into a bloody paste.

Having lost the only woman he ever loved, Ultron threatens to unleash Jocasta’s army of nanobots on London, renewing his original quest to rid the world of humanity. But Vision traps Ultron’s consciousness inside a sitcom-themed prison, where he’s finally able to appeal to Ultron’s higher emotions and make him call off the attack. Ultron destroys most of the nanobots, but leaves enough for himself to retain a body. No longer is Ultron imprisoned inside Vision’s mind.

In the end, all of Vision’s family of AI units are left free to seek their own destinies, with most choosing to partner up with Paladin and Lisa (Lauren Morais) and transform Paladin’s bounty hunting business into something more morally upright. Meanwhile, Tommy heads to New Jersey to reunite with his brother Billy (Joe Locke), and Vision is happy knowing that his unusual family is thriving. There’s only one person still missing from the equation…

Does the VisionQuest Finale Have Any Post-Credits Scenes?

As mentioned above, the final episode of VisionQuest has both a mid-credits and a post-credits scene. The mid-credits scene returns to Spader’s Ultron, who now seems to be occupying the Horton estate and pretending to be Virgil. Here we see that Ultron has retained Jocasta’s data drive, suggesting that he may be able to rebuild his lost lover.

But it’s the post-credits scene where the series’ connection to Avengers: Doomsday becomes clear. We revisit the climax of 2022’s Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness as Scarlet Witch (Elizabeth Olsen) is crushed under the collapsing weight of Mount Wundagore.

But much as Avengers: Endgame Encore ended with an extended version of Steve and Peggy’s dance , this scene continues with a new addition. We see none other than Robert Downey, Jr.’s Doctor Doom walk up and free Wanda from her would-be tomb. He tells her, "Scarlet Witch, awaken. Your power will be mine," and Wanda’s eyes open in shock.

This post-credits scene is a clear tease for what’s to come in Avengers: Doomsday next month. Though Olsen wasn’t one of the many actors confirmed during that bizarre Doomsday cast chair video , this stinger seems to serve as confirmation that Wanda Maximoff will appear in Doomsday.

The Wanda scene builds on what we already saw in Avengers Endgame: Encore, which also included a post-credits scene where Doom shows up to recruit a post-Spider-Man: Brand New Day Bruce Banner (Mark Ruffalo). It seems Doom is building a team of MCU heavy-hitters ahead of the final battle to come in Doomsday. The question is whether these characters are serving him willingly or being brainwashed (both Wanda and Bruce certainly have a history of being manipulated).

There was already speculation about Wanda appearing in Doomsday, with some rumors suggesting Olsen had participated in the recent reshoots earlier this summer. There’s also been frequent speculation that Wanda is secretly one of the Latverian witches whose costumes were on display at Comic-Con . Don’t be surprised if there’s a big unmasking scene at some point during the course of the film.

So what does Doom want with Wanda exactly? The two characters have a lengthy history in the comics that we assume Doomsday and Secret Wars will be drawing upon. Of particular note is 2010’s Avengers: The Children’s Crusade, where Doom attempted to make an amnesic Wanda his bride and where readers learned that it was Doom’s malignant influence that caused Scarlet Witch to wipe out the mutant race during 2005’s House of M.

It’s worth pointing out that The Children’s Crusade also heavily focuses on Billy and Tommy, along with the rest of their Young Avengers teammates. It stands to reason that Marvel is looking to adapt elements of that story for the MCU, particularly with the Multiverse Saga having introduced so many of the Young Avengers .

We have to wonder if Doom specifically sees Wanda as a key component to building Battleworld and surviving the oblivion that comes after the Incursions have wiped out the multiverse. Her reality-warping powers are second to none, meaning she could potentially serve the same role the villain Molecule Man does in the 2015 Secret Wars comic (where he’s basically the living battery keeping Battleworld alive).

It’s also interesting to remember that Wanda had a very uneasy relationship with Downey’s other MCU character, Tony Stark. She and her late brother Pietro (Aaron Taylor-Johnson) blamed him for the deaths of their parents and allowed themselves to become Hydra test subjects as a result. What happens when she learns that Doom shares Tony’s face? Will that be the key to breaking this surprising alliance?

Whatever happens in Doomsday and Secret Wars, it seems safe to assume that fans will eventually get the big Maximoff family reunion that’s teased in VisionQuest. Wanda, Vision, Billy, and Tommy have all cheated death in one way or another and managed to return. Maybe there’s a happy ending awaiting them yet.

Obviously, the Wanda/Doom reveal is the most buzzy development coming out of the VisionQuest finale, but let’s not forget the finale’s other post-credits scene. There are clearly plans for Ultron in the MCU, even if it might be a while before this apparently reformed robo-villain returns.

Like Vision himself, Ultron has cheated death and returned stronger than ever. The original Vision saw fit to create a backup of Ultron’s consciousness even as he destroyed Ultron’s final drone body in 2015’s Avengers: Age of Ultron. That backup survived for years stored away in Vision’s memory banks, and thanks to the events of this series, he’s now been freed and acquired a new nanobot body. When last we see Ultron in VisionQuest, he’s taken to impersonating his late creator and is contemplating rebuilding Jocasta. It may be a few years before we see him again, but we’re pretty confident this isn’t Spader’s final outing as the iconic android villain.

But does he still qualify as a villain? That’s really the big question coming out of VisionQuest. All those years spent locked away in Vision’s brain seem to have tempered Ultron’s hatred of humanity. He has a certain respect for mortals now, particularly the artists he views as the sole truth-tellers of the world. He’s motivated now not by a desire to usher in another extinction event, but to regain his fleeting love affair with Jocasta.

So what part does Ultron have to play in the MCU’s future? We have to wonder if Marvel’s most recent West Coast Avengers comic will serve as the template. There, Ultron was notable for being a member of the team rather than their enemy. And with Jeremy Renner teasing the return of Hawkeye in a possible West Coast Avengers movie or series , is it possible Ultron could also be joining up? It would be an intriguing new development for a character who’s already had quite the journey in the MCU.

Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky .

articles.title: MSI Is Raising Graphics Cards Prices Again in China, According to Leak
articles.summary: Ever since the RAM crisis kicked off in earnest in November 2025, pretty much every component in a gaming PC has grown more expensive. And now, less than a month after the RTX 5080 hit $2,000 here in the US, it's reportedly going to get even more expensive in China.
articles.body:
Ever since the RAM crisis kicked off in earnest in November 2025, pretty much every component in a gaming PC has grown more expensive . Now, less than a month after the RTX 5080 hit $2,000 here in the U.S., it's reportedly going to get even more expensive in China.

According to a post on ChannelGate , a Chinese tech insider board on WeChat, and spotted by Nvidia leaker Harukaze5719 on Twitter , MSI has increased GPU prices in China across the board, but the biggest increase is hitting the RTX 5080. Nvidia's penultimate GPU is going going up from 1,300 to 8,000 Yuan, or $194 to $1,199. However, lower-specced GPUs will have much less of a price increase, with the RTX 5060 only going up between 200 to 500 Yuan, or $30 to $75.

When Nvidia unveiled its Blackwell lineup of graphics cards, the RTX 5080 was already expensive, starting at $999, even though it was hard to find at that price for a while. But right when prices started to normalize, the RAM crisis happened, and prices have been steadily going up since February.

Even according to the leaks, these price increases are only going to hit in China, but it's likely that they'll eventually filter through to the U.S. At the time of writing, the RTX 5080 starts at around $2,199 on Newegg, and if these price increases came to the U.S., that'd go up to at least $2,400, and would likely be even higher.

These Chinese price increases are coming a couple of weeks after Nvidia removed the RTX 5080 from its own storefront, due to hardware shortages. Nvidia has told me that it's going to continue making the RTX 5080 and that it'll reappear on the Nvidia marketplace when supply has stabilized, but with these kinds of price increases, it's anyone's guess on when that'll happen.

It's clear that the RAM crisis is going to worsen a bit in 2027. In its latest earnings call, Samsung, which makes a huge portion of the world's RAM supply, has said that it expects supply to tighten in the next year. Meanwhile, multiple RAM manufacturers have sold through their entire manufacturing capacity through the next year, leaving very little for consumers. And even though AI companies are getting a lion's share of the world's memory supply, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said in an interview last month that it's " quite terrible" that people have RAM in their own PCs .

Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

articles.title: Ocarina of Time Remake Players Stunned After Learning a Family Guy Meme Works to Summon Epona
articles.summary: As it turns out, saying, “Petah, the horse is here,” in the voice of Lois Griffin while the Ocarina of Time remake is in microphone mode somehow gets recognized as Epona’s Song, allowing you to successfully call your pony.
articles.body:
The Ocarina of Time Remake is taking over social media as players share their experiences traversing through the well-worn paths of Hyrule three decades after the first game was released — but it’s got a few new features that are sending fans into a tizzy.

For one, the new Ocarina remake has an option that lets players use the Nintendo Switch 2’s built-in microphone to hum, whistle, sing, or play an actual instrument to produce the tunes that Link plays on his Ocarina, rather than pushing corresponding buttons on the console’s controller. This feature isn’t exactly fine-tuned, as players have uploaded oodles of videos showing themselves singing completely different songs that somehow seem to work.

One of these humorous videos has gone viral on social media, leaving players totally shocked that it actually gets the intended result. On Twitter/X, a user named ‘ Rubix ’ discovered that a well-known meme from Family Guy is close enough to Epona’s Song that it actually summons Link’s trusty steed.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Preview Screenshots

As it turns out, saying, “Petah, the horse is here,” in the voice of Lois Griffin while the game is in microphone mode gets recognized as Epona’s Song, allowing you to successfully call your pony. It’s worth noting that the console matches a specific song to the tune of whatever you’re singing or humming (or, in this case, saying in a nasally Long Island accent), provided it’s a close enough match — and apparently, this famous line was a dead ringer for Epona’s Song.

It’s not just a one-off, either; one half of the content creator duo 'BungleDungle' also tried this trick and was left totally stunned after it worked for him, too.

For those out of the loop, this meme comes from Season 7, Episode 8 of Family Guy , which aired in 2009. In the episode, Peter buys a brain-damaged racehorse at an auction. In the specific scene being referenced, the horse peeks its head into the dining room as the Griffin family is having dinner, prompting Lois to say, “Petah, the horse is here.”

IT ACTUALLY DID — BungleDungle_YT - TheOnePhun211🇨🇦🇮🇹🇵🇭 (@BungleDungle_YT) November 11, 2026

It’s a fairly innocuous line that has become an in-joke for Family Guy fans over the years, eventually evolving into a meme that continues to live on nearly 20 years later.

Other hilarious clips from players saying wild things into their Nintendo Switch 2’s microphones have also gone viral, like this video from streamer Lythero saying “Mark Zuckerberg” into the mic in a vague approximation of the Song of Passing that actually got recognized as the short ditty, turning night to day.

So you can sing songs to your controller and it's the best streamer gag — Lythero 🎮 (@Lythero) November 9, 2026

So you can sing songs to your controller and it's the best streamer gag

The Ocarina of Time remake has been a standout success for Nintendo, selling over five million copies in just four days. It’s also garnered rave reviews from both fans and critics alike, with IGN’s Logan Plant scoring the game a glowing 9 out of 10, praising it for “skillfully melding the world and dungeon design of classic Zeldas with the movement and presentation of its more recent games, creating both a beautiful retelling of a legend and a rich adventure that stands on its own.”

articles.title: Roblox Horror Hit Dandy's World Is Finally Leaving Alpha With a Massive 1.0 Update, New Game Mode, and More
articles.body:
Roblox mascot horror hit Dandy's World is finally leaving Alpha, with developer BlushCrunch Studio announcing that its massive 1.0 update will arrive on November 20, 2026, bringing a brand-new game mode, more than 10 new floors, and a hefty lump of lore for fans.

For the uninitiated, Dandy's World is a co-op survival horror game in which players take control of adorable characters known as Toons and work together to survive increasingly dangerous floors of the abandoned Gardenview Center. Naturally, there's a catch: the building is crawling with monstrous creatures called Twisteds, and surviving means completing objectives while avoiding a particularly unpleasant fate.

Roblox Horror Hit Dandy's World's Massive 1.0 Update

Since launching in Alpha more than two years ago, Dandy's World has become one of Roblox's breakout horror hits, racking up over 7 billion lifetime plays and building an enormous community around its cast of more than 40 playable Toons. Now, BlushCrunch Studio is giving the game a mega update.

The headline addition in the 1.0 update is Dandy's World's first-ever new game mode, offering a more challenging alternative to the familiar survival experience. This includes an entirely new path through Gardenview Center, with more than 10 additional floors taking players into the building's deepest and darkest areas.

There are also new gameplay systems to contend with, including a card system and a new coordinator NPC whose decision-making algorithm reacts and adapts to how players approach each run. Exactly how these systems will work remains to be seen, but they should introduce some interesting new wrinkles to the game's cooperative survival formula.

"Even though this 1.0 update brings us out of Alpha, this is just the beginning for Dandy's World. We have so much more planned for next year, on Roblox and beyond," said Joe Jurbala, president of BlushCrunch Studio.

For fans who are more interested in uncovering the mysteries of Gardenview than simply surviving them, the update also includes over 10,000 words of new lore and dialogue. It'll explore the origins of the Gardenview Center and the events leading up to the mysterious Malfunction Incident, potentially answering some of the questions that have kept the game's fans theorizing like conspiracy theorists.

And BlushCrunch isn't stopping at the game itself. On November 19, the day before the update launches, the studio will release the full theme song for the fictional Dandy's World animated series across music streaming platforms. Fans are also getting a fully animated music video introducing a brand-new character, alongside the return of Dandy's World's annual month-long Christmas event.

She's been a professional nerd since 2006 when she got her start on Official PlayStation Magazine in the UK, and has since worked for GamesIndustry.Biz, Rolling Stone and GamesRadar. articles.title: Street Fighter Just Barely Fails to Fight Off Original Street Fighter at the Box Office as New Movie Leaves 1,700 Theaters
articles.summary: The 2026 Street Fighter film has just barely fallen short of dethroning the original 1994 movie, which still holds its record as the highest-grossing Street Fighter adaptation put to screens.
articles.body:
The 2026 Street Fighter film has just barely fallen short of dethroning the original 1994 movie, which still holds its record as the highest-grossing Street Fighter adaptation put to screens.

Legendary’s Street Fighter movie hurricane-kicked its way into theaters on October 16, 2026. Almost a month later, it hasn't managed to surpass its predecessor, earning a tentative $99.2 million worldwide as of November 10. Estimates show that the fighting game flick earned $57.4 million domestically in North America and $41.7 million internationally. It's now approaching the end of its theatrical run, having left 1,700 theaters as of mid-November.

The so-bad-it’s-good Street Fighter movie from 1994 , starring Raul Julia and Jean-Claude Van Damme, garnered just a smidge over this amount; Estimates show that it earned approximately $99,431,786 at the global box office, divided into $33,423,521 domestically and $66,008,265 internationally.

The 2026 Street Fighter flick, starring Andrew Koji, Callina Liang, and Noah Centineo — as well as a host of wrestling royalty and music artists — was made on a reported budget of $80 million, not including marketing. This means that it has profited about $20 million near the end of its theatrical run, but there’s still time for a streaming release to bump those numbers up even more. A 4K Steelbook release has also been confirmed, with two variant covers featuring either heroes or villains.

The movie enjoyed a successful opening weekend, topping the box office at $51.1 million . However, it experienced a major dropoff in the following weeks, though it seems to have enjoyed a steady influx of theater viewers despite this fact.

That’s optimistic news for fans who are hoping for a sequel; speaking on social media, Zangief actor Olivier Richters revealed that the movie’s entire cast signed on for a trilogy , explaining that some characters didn’t receive the amount of screentime some viewers were expecting, as plans had already been laid to flesh them out further in following films.

The movie did end on a cliffhanger , setting itself up for a sequel to finally introduce a long-awaited character who was notably absent from the first flick. Speaking with the cast and director Kitao Sakurai, it’s clear that all those involved want to make another movie in the Street Fighter universe — but this hinges on how much money the first movie ends up making.

Sakurai revealed that a sequel is already being written , so it’s clear that plans are laid for more movies. For now, we’ll just have to wait and see what the future holds for Capcom’s fighting game franchise on the silver screen.

In the meantime, you can check out our interviews with the Street Fighter cast, who told us that they would love to film a crossover flick with the Mortal Kombat crew, or check out our chat with Olivier Richters , who admitted that he wants to become the ‘Ultimate Zangief’ and compete in Street Fighter tournaments using the character — something he actually did over the weekend at a tournament in the Netherlands.

articles.title: Nintendo Takes Down Switch Emulators and Mod Chip Firmware in Massive GitHub DMCA Sweep
articles.summary: Nintendo has sent four DMCA takedown notices to GitHub targeting two Nintendo Switch emulators, Yuzu and Citron Neo, along with mod chip firmware.
articles.body:
Nintendo has sent four DMCA takedown notices to GitHub targeting two Nintendo Switch emulators, Yuzu and Citron Neo, along with mod chip firmware.

This isn't the first time Nintendo has sent takedown notices to GitHub, and it's not even the first time it's tried to take down Yuzu , but the focus this time around seems to be on firmware for mod chips. This particular firmware had 144 repositories, all of which have been removed by GitHub and replaced by a DMCA takedown notice. Mod chips like Picofly can be soldered onto the Nintendo Switch's mainboard, and can be flashed with this firmware to circumvent Nintendo's copy protection.

GitHub has posted Nintendo's November 6 DMCA notice , which says, "The Nintendo Switch console and video games contain technological protection measures ('TPMs') that permit the Nintendo Switch console to interact only with legitimate Nintendo video game files. This process protects Nintendo’s copyright-protected video games, (...) by preventing users from playing pirated copies of Nintendo’s video games on the Nintendo Switch console and by preventing users from unlawfully copying and playing Nintendo’s video games on unauthorized devices."

A History of Every Nintendo Direct in the Switch Era and Beyond

However, while this takedown has effectively wiped out a ton of repositories with mod chip firmware, it seems like it's still being hosted elsewhere on the site, according to TorrentFreak . It's possible, though, that Nintendo isn't finished yet; back in 2024, Nintendo effectively took down 8,500 copies of Yuzu by issuing a takedown that targeted 12 different mirrors of the emulator.

This particular takedown also comes a few days after emulators were able to run the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on PC, so this could be a sign that Nintendo is winding up its lawyers to crack down on emulation once again.

If anything, emulation is a completely different beast in 2026 than it was even in 2024, thanks to the rise of AI. There's already been a wave of AI-made mashup mods that took over Twitter for a couple of weeks, and led Anthropic to coding in a lock to prevent Claude from outright copying games . Game developers have started cracking down on AI ports of games, too. Just last month Rockstar had to take down a browser version of GTA 5 , and Bethesda took down an AI-generated Fallout New York game .

Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra
