articles.title: Tanuki: Pon's Summer Brings Back BMX Freestyle as a Cute Mail Delivery Adventure | IGN Review
articles.summary: While some parts of Tanuki: Pon's Summer don't live up to what makes it special, it still captures the vibe of summer wrapped in a fun BMX delivery service.
articles.body:
Frost hasn't yet replaced New England's morning dew, but cold air is starting to settle in. Days feel short, and the sun sets before I've signed off from work for the day. I complain all summer about the heat, then want it back just as it starts to fade: Long, meandering days that are full of potential. It feels fitting – and maybe a bit ironic – that as soon as my mind (and maybe yours) starts wandering back to summer, Kyoto-based studio Denkiworks released its homage to summer in rural Japan with Tanuki: Pon's Summer. It's a game that feels just as warm as the summer depicted, and a nice reprieve from the looming cold.

Tanuki: Pon's Summer is set in an idyllic Japanese countryside that's centered around an aging shrine. Pon, the tanuki tasked with tending to it, let the shrine's grounds crumble while he ate chips and played video games. Tanuki gods bully Pon into getting his act together and fixing the shrine before a big festival. But that'll cost money, and money comes from a job. Pon's skills are limited, but he does have a BMX bike. To the post office it is! You play through a month of Pon's summer, delivering the island's mail to earn money to fix the shrine, and days are all marked on a calendar. Along the way, it so perfectly captures the lazy opportunity of summer in its moment-to-moment about a relaxed town.

The island is not big, but it's quite dense with several distinct, lively parts of town and Pon must figure out how to get around efficiently on his bike. (You can walk; Pon can't jump on foot, but can on his bike, so walking for even short distances is not effective.) Conveniently, the island is bike-friendly, especially BMX bike-friendly with the makings of a skatepark. So, delivering mail is not just a thing you do – it's the draw.

Each day, Pon picks up the mail from the post office, stacking them in a basket through a Tetris-like minigame that feels like a welcome ritual each in-game day. Then, he heads out. Tanuki: Pon's Summer is open-world in the sense that you can make deliveries in any order, but the storyline is linear. Some of the packages are simple dropoffs, but others have an activity or a storyline attached to them and to the people of the island. Among them are rival sushi and yakitori chefs, a creatively-stifled photographer, and a tough guy with a soft spot. All of these characters are delightfully weird, and their stories follow suit.

Those rival chefs, for instance, have some longstanding beef between each other, and aren't initially very nice to Pon, either. They know him as a lazy tanuki who let the shrine crumble, and throughout Pon's month as a mailman, their attitudes toward each other (and Pon!) soften. Pon's adventure, too, helps reunite an estranged father and daughter, who are both artisan makers. Tanuki: Pon's Summer may have Pon in the name, but it's hardly Pon's story that's being told. It's a charming one that's more focused on the relationships between people on the island and the community they make together.

Crucially, each of these island residents needs help with something, which is where Tanuki: Pon's Summer's minigames come in. And there are a lot, like skewering meat and veggies to make yakitori, stacking pieces of sushi to order, sanding logs, serving shaved ice and foamy beer, checking out customers at the convenience store, playing the drums for a local musician, hitting home runs at the local baseball field. Minigames like these (and a bunch others) mimic that sort of delight of childhood summers in which anything seemed possible. They're the sorts of small adventures that break up drifting days in the summer heat.

But not all of these minigames are as joyous, though. Several of them feel like a monotonous drag where Pon sands down logs at a snail's pace or another that forces Pon to cut down far too many bamboo stalks. Sure, we had to do chores on a summer break, but I resented some of the minigames for taking me away from the excitement of riding Pon's bike around town and many of the other things I'd have rather been doing.

You could put all sorts of descriptors on it, whether that's a mail delivery simulator, a BMX freestyle game, or a cooking game. And oftentimes, this approach brought a lot of whimsy and a steady variety from moment to moment. But there were a bit too many where I wanted Tanuki: Pon's Summer to let me get back to the thing I liked most about the game: Riding around on Pon's bike.

The core of Tanuki: Pon's Summer is getting from place to place on his bike while making an extreme sport out of it. He bunny hops over small cliffs, grinds down handrails, and pulls off tricks over gaps and soars over sunny rooftops. Tricks are simple enough to pull off by directional stick movements and button inputs while in air, but stringing them together for combos is a bit more tricky. Optional challenges dotted around the island offer a chance to test your skill, but otherwise the game doesn't ask Pon to prove himself, aside from the occasional request where a resident asks Pon to do some tricks, under a time limit, to reach a certain number of points. (All tricks amass points, which typically don't mean anything. It pops up on screen even if you're doing a barspin into a wheelie on your way to just deliver a model kit.) It doesn't necessarily need to ask, because the BMX freestyle itself is a blast. On deliveries, I longed for long stretches of road to see how far I could make Pon wheelie. I used helpfully placed ramps to look for new routes and bounced from roof top to roof top just to show off.

The worst of Tanuki: Pon's Summer's minigames either lingered for too long or felt dull compared to the fun of his bike. Although they are relatively short, those select minigames (emphasis on mini) dragged in a way that broke up the momentum I'd have from riding around town and doing tricks on my way to the next delivery. Most of them don't repeat – Pon is asked once, for instance, to balance and roll boulders through a tricky maze or to pour the perfect beers from a bar's tap. Once Pon's done, he's done. He's moved on to the next task, and whoever asked for his help won't ask him to do that particular chore again, but they may ask for some other sort of help.

The last piece of Tanuki: Pon's Summer to talk about is the shrine decor, which is entirely optional. People who enjoyed decorating their Animal Crossing: New Horizons islands may be drawn to this in particular. Slowly, more of the shrine opens up big, empty swaths of land you can decorate – up to you whether or not it's worthwhile. Pon collects decor and furniture from the quests he's set upon by islanders, but he can also purchase stuff from the kitsune lingering around. His overarching goal is about getting the shrine together for the big festival, but the decorating simulator felt extraneous for me. There's no real parameters here to guide the direction or to make the feature feel consequential in any way – it's just something to do. Again, it felt like a slower piece of the game that took me away from the parts I liked best.

Playing through Tanuki: Pon's Summer took about 10 hours. Most of this time was following the storyline, doing challenges, and messing around on the bike, but some of this time was redoing days lost from game-breaking pre-release bugs. The autosave feature is not so generous, and it'd be smart to make frequent use of the manual save feature in case bugs persist past the launch window.

articles.title: Amazon's Early Black Friday Manga Sale Includes Multiple Generations of Box Sets
articles.body:
Black Friday is still several weeks away, but Amazon is already unloading physical media deals. I’m the first to admit I read most manga online these days, so when I do buy a physical copy, it’s likely something I already love. Enter the box set, which seems to be a major focus of Amazon’s early Black Friday discounts .

Box sets were massive back in the day, but publishers like Viz Media and Shout Factory are still keeping the trend alive. They collect full arcs and at times an entire series, making it easy to binge or go back through your favorite panels. A solid box keeps things organized, and most sets come with some kind of collectible bonus.

I've been scrolling through Amazon’s manga deals and found new low prices on classic shonen collections as well as some popular new releases.

One Piece Box Set: East Blue and Baroque Works, Volumes 1-23

Like I said, some of the best deals are on the classics. One Piece, the best-selling manga of all time, has a number of different box sets on the market. If you somehow haven’t already started your journey, the first (treasure) box set collects 23 volumes of the East Blue and Baroque Works (also known as Alabasta Saga) arcs, lining up with about how far the Netflix series has gotten in its first two seasons.

An ongoing manga with over 1,000 chapters may sound daunting, but I promise it’s one of the greats for a reason. The first box set is currently at its lowest price of the year at $161 , adding up to around $7 per volume. If you’re working on a full collection, later box sets are getting similar discounts.

Chainsaw Man Box Set: Includes volumes 1-11

My Hero Academia Box Set 1: Includes volumes 1-20

Ouran High School Host Club Complete Box Set

On the more recent side of things, we’re seeing an a new low price on the Chainsaw Man box set , which collects all 97 chapters of the Public Safety Arc. The hefty Jujutsu Kaisen set collects all 30 volumes of the manga, including volume 0. Both of these come with a good ol’ poster.

My Hero Academia's collector's box set comes with the first 20 volumes, featuring cover art that was originally exclusive to Japan. It also comes with an exclusive 48-page booklet of illustrations in addition to the usual poster, and would make a great pick-up for any fans missing the now-finished anime .

And, of course, I haven’t forgotten about the shojo lovers. I highly recommend the Ouran High School Host Club box set I currently have sitting on my shelf. It collects all 18 volumes of Bisco Hatori’s manga, which is one of the funniest things I’ve ever read. Instead of a poster, the box set gifts you a pretty cute notepad with illustrations of the Host Club members. Amazon's early Black Friday deal has brought the full set under $100 .

I’ve been covering Amazon sales for several years now, and have become keenly aware of how the retailer handles its deals. One thing I’ve consistently seen is that whatever Amazon labels "early Black Friday deals" don’t tend to get any better on the actual day. However, there’s two caveats I’d keep in mind as you shop:

First, Amazon is prone to surprise-dropping BOGO sales that often include manga and other physical media. We don’t know for sure whether one of those sales will happen over Black Friday, but if it does, that would offer even more savings (assuming you pick up multiple volumes or sets).

The other caveat is Amazon’s aggressive price-matching. While Amazon might not plan to drop these prices any lower, if another retailer does, Amazon will be quick to make sure their own listing is one cent lower. Yep, it’s a whole thing.

Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

articles.title: The Rings of Power Stars React to This Week's Big Season 3 Deaths
articles.summary: Showrunners Patrick McKay and J.D. Payne and the stars of The Rings of Power discuss this week's big Season 3 deaths: ‘It was the correct, if painful, end of their journeys.’
articles.body:
Full spoilers follow for Episodes 1-4 of Season 3 of The Rings of Power , which are streaming now on Prime Video.

Just four episodes into Season 3 of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power , and showrunners Patrick McKay and J.D. Payne have already delivered two consequential deaths from their pool of original Middle-earth characters. In “The Gift of Men,” Ema Horvath’s Eärien, Elendil's daughter, takes her own life rather than allow King Pharazôn (Trystan Gravelle) to punish her. And “Gundabad” ends with the tragic, lifeless eyes of Elven warrior Arondir (Ismael Cruz Córdova) staring out across the wasteland of Morodor.

The series has never shied away from killing characters, but McKay told IGN this season’s deaths are about underscoring how Sauron and his evil are ascendant. “There are real stakes,” he explained. “There is a real cost to what Sauron is doing. As we were in the writers’ room, myself and J.D., very early on, we felt that the audience needed to feel that and feel it viscerally. We had to take things from the audience. It had to hurt.”

In Episode 2, it’s revealed that Eärien has convincingly played the part of enthusiastic King Pharazôn stan and Númenórean purist, while she’s actually been a mole for exiled queen regent and Faithful Havens leader Míriel (Cynthia Addai-Robinson). For five years, she fed Númenor’s movements and plans to her brother Isildur (Maxim Baldry).

“She helped her father escape arrest, and that's supposed to be a real turning point for that character,” McKay said of Eärien’s change in worldview this season. “She's now essentially a spy within the enemy camp trying to protect people like her, trying to protect her family, and she feels incredibly guilty that she was in part responsible for bringing these people to power.”

McKay cited the shocking death of Marion Crane (Janet Leigh) in Psycho as their inspiration for how to frame Eärien’s exit. “The idea [was] that we would open up Númenor with this is all about Eärien and she’s a double agent and she's feeling it deeply, and she's feeling the walls closing in around her,” he explained. “And then, we'll take her away from you just as you're getting used to her as a character in the situation. We felt that that would disrupt the narrative and shock the audience a little bit.”

Though her death will be an audience shock, actress Ema Horvath told IGN that she knew from the very beginning that Eärien would never leave the island. “I knew that in some sense the entire parable of Númenor was gonna be kind of contained within her character. But I didn't know exactly how or when I was gonna go, and so that was new information to me.”

She said McKay and Payne pitched her the storyline in a Zoom call before she flew to the UK to film Season 3. “They're very good at animating the world for you,” Horvath remembered. “So they got to the end of what happened and I was so into the story that I got off the Zoom and my husband was like, ‘Did you hear what they said? Did you not process it, because you're not behaving like the way someone would react to that information?’ And so it did take me a couple hours to just process that that was the end of my time on the show. But I was very excited about the story side of it.”

Having given birth to her first child between Seasons 2 and 3, Horvath said that “deepened my work, I think, drastically. There are parts of myself that are way more accessible that have been hidden for a while, and then new ones that have cropped up. This season I had the most fun shooting because of that.”

She described Eärien by this season as a woman very good at acting the part but battling with unbearable “shame” for her actions. “I think if you watch it once – this is my hope – you see someone terrible at the beginning,” said the actress. “And I think if you watch it again, what's behind the eyes is a little different. You're watching a severely depressed person with massive amounts of shame. If someone watches it that is coming from Season 2 and thinks she's fully committed to the cause, maybe on a second watch they can see the sadness.”

All it takes is just one messy reconnaissance mission in Belzagar’s (Will Keen) private quarters to tip off her true mission, and she’s then confronted by the trifecta of hate: Belzagar, Pharazôn and his weaselly son, Kemen (Leon Wadham).

“I love the shape of that scene, because she's still trying,” Horath said. “She’s trying until the very end to appeal to [Kemen] and she appeals to [Belzagar] in a different way. And then I was most excited about getting to act with Trystan. We’ve never delivered lines to each other and we finally got to do it,” she smiled. “But then there's a moment where she's not even in the room anymore.”

Eärien just turns from the men who are thrilled that they’ve caged her and she walks out the window and drops to her death. Director Charlotte Brändström explained to IGN, “I remember when I shot it on set, a cameraman was pushing to follow her to the window. I said, ‘No, no, that would feel wrong… I don't want to feel the intention.’ We just stayed wide and she slowly walked away and just jumped. And then, you cut to their reactions, and… it just felt right to me.”

Horvath agreed, “Charlotte and I were really on the same page with that walk to the window. Obviously, you're thinking in terms of surprise. But even on a psychological level, after the research I had done, that tracked with what that can look like.

“When someone no longer has power over you — and I don't think these people have really had power over her for a while because this choice has been on the table for a long time for her — she didn't know if she was ever gonna have to use it,” the actress said. “The mask is off at this moment and [they] really have no power over me. There are forces and ideas and things that are way more important and I think that's so much more powerful than getting into an argument with someone. When you're no longer arguing with someone, there’s tremendous power in that.”

The Death of Arondir, the Wood Elf Who Became a Warrior

The second massive loss comes at the end of “Gundabad” with Arondir’s unexpected reunion with his human lover’s son, Theo (Tyroe Muhafidin), a recently conscripted Nazgnagôl for Sauron.

“The idea of the journey that Theo goes on and the journey that Arondir goes on, having their paths intersect in a way that has ultimately tragic consequences, that was one of the earliest ideas that we kind of hung the whole season around,” McKay said of this long-planned, fateful moment.

At least for Arondir actor Ismael Cruz Córdova, it takes four episodes to get to there, which means his character gets plenty to do this season before his end – including more death-defying battles and embarking on an emotionally eventful road trip with Galadriel (Morfydd Clark) and the orc Marnûkh (Adam Young).

Córdova shared with IGN that Arondir’s “dark night of the soul” exploration in the last two seasons of Rings of Power have paralleled his own personal journey: “I definitely allow what happens in my life to go through my work. It's the way that I've been able to live and grieve and grow. I was going through quite a moment in my own life shooting Season 2, and going into Season 3 I was dealing with sickness from a parent. He's good now but at that moment it was tough.

“And I was told that the character wouldn't be coming back the same day that my dad got his diagnosis, so that put me right there. I'm sheepish about talking about these personal things because I don't want to be exploiting them for the story, but this is how it happened. And when we were gonna shoot the death sequence — it was like a six-day sequence — the day before that, one of the loves of my life passed away in a car crash as well, so those bookends were so sharp.”

The actor said he was grateful that, before his character was killed off, the showrunners allowed Arondir to build a real friendship with Galadriel where they could challenge one another, and come to understand the orcs through Marnûkh.

“One of the things that I told the showrunners when they told me Arondir’s fate, I said, ‘Well, if he's gonna go, let's make sure that we can show all the colors of him, things that we haven't seen, things that we want to punch up, and that people can see a little bit more of him in the softer side,’” Córdova said. “You see all that, and you see that softness with Marnûkh, and you see that friendliness with Galadriel. But on a drop of a hat, I will obliterate [any foes too].

“We saw this little outcast that was out there all muddied up, carrying out tasks for who knows who that he never met,” he continued. “And now I'm at that same table telling them what to do in terms of military strategy. Still wearing the same costume.”

As for that never-changing Arondir costume, the actor chuckled: “I would say, that was a creative choice of a certain kind. I'm not sure exactly what that is, but for me, how I see it is like, ‘I'm gonna go through this entire thing and I'm gonna do it my way, and I'm gonna be on your table dressing exactly how I came from and representing.’ And he does.”

Regarding the fateful, final collision of Sauron, Theo and Arondir, Córdova said he worried most for Tyroe Muhafidin. “He is just a piece of my heart. He's family,” he said. “I've seen him grow from 14 years old and now he's a grown man, taller than me.”

The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 Photos

It was difficult for Muhafidin to be the one who pierces Arondir with his sword in the end.

“Tyro was struggling with having to be the one who would take him away. He was really struggling with that,” Córdova said.

“I think when we were shooting, he was having a harder time than me, so I had to caregive in that moment,” he continued. “I think it was the same with Arondir and Theo. I wanted Theo and Tyro to know that Arondir and Ismael knew that it wasn't his fault. I'm out here having trouble with it [now] but that’s truly what I was consistently thinking. [Theo] has had all of the things happen to him, and he still has fought and fought and fought. Even at that moment, I just wanted him to know that I love him. Period. I loved him and I believed in them. That's it.”

McKay said both actors were “pros” about their deaths and understood the importance of their character’s sacrifices. “Both Ema and Ismael were absolutely on board and absolutely saw what we were going for and saw why it was the correct, if painful, end of their journeys in this regard. I think both of those stories are really powerful, and I think both of their performances are incredible.”

articles.title: New GTA 6 Surprise Gameplay Seemingly Released in Yet Another Viral Marketing Stunt
articles.summary: Rockstar Games appears to have released new footage from GTA 6, which also recreates the studio's real-life viral marketing in-game.
articles.body:
Rockstar Games appears to have released new footage from GTA 6 , which also recreates the studio's real-life viral marketing in-game.

A new Instagram post from the account "Only in Dade" began to raise eyebrows earlier today, as it appeared to contain legitimate footage of GTA 6. The footage shows someone driving down Ocean Drive, recording a bunch of flashy cars lined up while people wander past. A second person on the sidewalk recorded the exact same video from a different perspective. Some fans think that the two people recording are Jason and Lucia, respectively, though the footage isn't clear enough to be able to confidently make that determination.

Many were wondering if this was AI footage or a render until Rockstar Games reposted it on its Instagram story and liked the video, indicating this is likely real in-game footage. The studio is very careful and calculated with what it chooses to post and interact with, so it isn't going around liking random AI-generated clips of its upcoming game.

However, what's even more interesting is that this footage directly recreates a real-life video from last month. Rockstar teamed up with West Coast Customs to bring cars from GTA 6 to real life and spent October parading them around the city of Miami. As a result, there were tons of videos and social media posts about these vehicles, and one has now seemingly been recreated in GTA 6. You can see the same people, including a person on a motorized scooter and a man taking pictures in front of one of the cars, all replicated in the GTA 6 footage above.

It's clear that Rockstar's marketing strategy has gotten extremely creative, and it's a bit of a flex to produce something that has many wondering if the visuals are too good to be true. Rockstar also pulled off a similar stunt a couple of weeks ago when it debuted a tiny bit of new gameplay during an episode of South Park . The footage wasn't advertised ahead of time, so people also thought that it might be AI-generated gameplay until Rockstar's name was discovered in the credits.

The hype for GTA 6 is currently at its peak, releasing in just one week. The launch represents the end of a 13-year journey for many fans, as Rockstar hasn't made a new GTA game since 2013. There was, of course, Red Dead Redemption 2 in 2018, which certainly helped tide some fans over... but that was still nearly a decade ago at this point.

Pre-loading has officially begun so fans can prepare for their trip to Vice City next week. Rockstar has also released new trailers , screenshots , and other marketing beats, which have created a flury of speculation over what may or may not be in the game . Thankfully, we won't have to wait much longer to find out.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: CD Projekt Red Used AI to Alter Geralt's Voice Due to Polish Actor's Health Issues
articles.summary: The Witcher 3 is getting a new expansion more than 11 years after it first released, and due to a health issue experienced by Geralt's Polish voice actor, CD Projekt Red will be using an AI tool to modify his voice.
articles.body:
The Witcher 3 is getting a new expansion more than 11 years after it first released, and due to a health issue experienced by Geralt's Polish voice actor, CD Projekt Red will be using an AI tool to modify his voice.

Jacek Rozenek, who voiced Geralt in The Witcher 3's Polish dub, will be returning to voice Geralt in Songs of the Past . Rozenek notably suffered a stroke back in 2019 that affected his voice. Thanks to modern technology, CD Projekt Red is able to use an AI voice modulator, Respeecher, to alter the actor's voice to match his 2014 lines, as noted by Game File .

According to the post, Rozenek's stroke left him unable to even speak for a while, and he only gained his voice back after a ton of rigorous training. He was able to return for a couple of quests in the Next-Gen update that came out back in 2022, but told Game File that he "was so exhausted after this recording." Still, CD Projekt Red wanted him to return for the new expansion, so it had to think outside the box.

The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past screenshots

The main problem was that, after everything Rozenek went through, his voice was noticably different than it was in 2014 when he recorded the bulk of Geralt's lines for the original game. Rozenek's voice is now much lower pitched than it used to be, which would make any new lines sound odd when played next to the older ones that are supposed to take place in the same time period. Hence, the need for Respeecher.

Respeecher's model was trained on all of Rozenek's lines from the original game, but it sounds like this was doing a lot more than just running his voice through a quick filter. When asked about the process, Respeecher synthetic speech artist Dmytro Vasylets told Game File that "getting there took dozens of hours, training models, going through the details with the CDPR team, and dealing with AI artifacts that never fully disappear."

CDPR got Rozenek's blessing to use the tool, who told Game File, "I have great trust… for the creators of this game," and that, "when it comes to the dynamics of the voice, when it comes to the acting aspects, I feel very good, really very good."

Still, CDPR is aware of the optics of using AI anywhere near a voice actor, and it stressed to Game File that this was a special case. CD Projekt Red localization producer Mikołaj Szwed told the publication that the company wouldn't be using any AI tools to alter someone's voice without the express permission of that voice actor.

Even for The Witcher 4 , which Rozenek is expected to return for, the tool won't be needed, due to Geralt being older and more grizzled, so a deeper voice won't be so jarring.

But while this seems like a good use of AI, the technology is still extremely controversial in gaming. Last year, the Indie Game Awards stripped the Game of the Year award from Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 after AI-generated placeholder textures were found in the game . Players have also found AI-generated art in Crimson Desert, though it's since been patched out.

articles.title: Final Fantasy XIV Players Mourn The Primals Bassist With In-Game Funerals and Gatherings
articles.summary: Final Fantasy XIV players are paying tribute to the bassist of the game’s official band, mourning him and celebrating his legacy with virtual, in-game funerals across servers worldwide.
articles.body:
Final Fantasy XIV players are paying tribute to the bassist of the game’s official band, mourning him and celebrating his legacy with virtual, in-game funerals across servers worldwide.

Eikichi Iwai was the bass guitarist for The Primals, a band formed specifically to make some of the music in Square Enix’s extremely popular MMORPG. While they aren’t the only ones responsible for some of the game’s iconic tunes, they’re certainly some of the most notable, and they’ve become a firm fixture in the Final Fantasy fanbase over the years.

Iwai’s death was officially announced on November 11, 2026 by his own rock band, Chirinuruwowa, and the Final Fantasy XIV development team, the latter of which penned a public letter to fans informing them of the news.

Final Fantasy XIV Lore Interview - The Development Team

“As announced earlier today, we are deeply saddened to share the news of the sudden passing of bassist Eikichi Iwai,” the statement reads. “Having witnessed his truly unforgettable performance on stage at the recent FINAL FANTASY XIV Fan Festival in Japan, the sudden news of his passing has come as a profound shock. The members of THE PRIMALS and the entire FFXIV Development and Operations teams are overcome with deep sorrow.

“As we reflect on all that Eikichi-san has left behind, our thoughts are with him, and we offer our heartfelt condolences.”

Chirinuruwowa published a similar statement on social media. “We regret to inform you that our bassist, Iwaieikichi, has passed away suddenly,” the group wrote. “The sudden news of his passing has left all of us in the band and on the staff struggling to come to terms with it, and we are deeply saddened.” The band also informed fans that all upcoming performances in their Endless Loop 2026 -Public- tour have been cancelled.

Iwai's death sent shockwaves throughout the FFXIV playerbase. In acknowledgement of his legacy as a performer and paying tribute to his contributions to the game, these players gathered together within their respective servers to hold virtual funerals in some of the MMORPG’s fantastical locales.

For example, players on the European server Omega formed a circle around Limsa Lominsa’s Aetheryte Plaza, lighting campfires in remembrance of the bassist. And in the Sephirot, Materia DC server, players hung out for more than seven hours at Ultima Thule, calmly sitting in its field of flowers.

Fans, content creators, and fellow members of the games industry have shared their own fond memories of the game and the impact Iwai's music had on their lives.

articles.title: Jamie Campbell Bower Calls Rings of Power Season 3 the 'Perfect Kind of Antidote' After Stranger Things
articles.summary: The character of Celeborn -- Jamie Campbell Bower's first role after playing Vecna, et al, in Seasons 4 and 5 of Stranger Things -- helped the actor move on from those persistently dark characters.
articles.body:
Jamie Campbell Bower has not been coy about Stranger Things being an emotionally taxing gig. As Vecna (and all of his many iterations) in the final two seasons of the Netflix series, Bower would put himself through intense and isolating experiences in preparation of playing the show's big bad. At MegaCon in early 2025, months ahead of the Stranger Things series finale, Bower said that he told his therapist that he wouldn't "be doing another bad guy for a minute" because it "f---s me up."

Bower's first post-Stranger Things role is, appropriately, miles away from his characters' persistent darkness. He's now starring in the third season of Prime Video's Rings of Power , which picks up five years after Season 2 well into the battle with Sauron, as Galadriel's long-lost husband, the elf Celeborn . Morfydd Clark's Galadriel mentions in Season 1 that Celeborn had not returned from his battle with Morgoth. In Season 3, the semi-estranged couple is reunited. On the red carpet for the season premiere in New York, Bower said that playing Celeborn was refreshing.

"I've been describing it as the perfect kind of antidote, I suppose," he told IGN. "It is so different to what I was doing before, and I'm so grateful to be here and so grateful to join this amazing cast and crew and this world. It's been beautiful. It really has been. It's been gorgeous."

Bower also elaborated on playing a character who has more ambiguity. J.R.R. Tolkien wrote several versions of Celeborn's origins, but never settled on one definitively. Thanks to the murkiness of of Tolkien's legendarium, the many depictions of Celeborn in adapted media and Tolkien's own writings left room for the actor to interpret the elf in his own way.

"Celeborn's really interesting because he was approached and then kind of re-approached in the works. And so there has been sort of... not conflicting, but different information that's available on him," he said. "My job was realistically to take what was there, look at what I related to, look at what was obvious, and then build on top of that. And I think for me as an actor, my intention was really to come into it with sensitivity and a vulnerability for him, which has been beautiful. It's been great."

We haven't seen too much of Celeborn in Season 3 yet, only appearing in a flashback meeting Galadriel 1,000 years ago in Episode 1 and again in Episode 4 (no spoilers), but it sure seems freeing to be able to act without prosthetics from day one.

We're liking Season 3 so far, giving the first batch of episodes an 8 in our review and calling it "a new beginning for the Prime Video series [...], streamlining the overall narrative into a more cohesive war story" that "refocuses The Rings of Power on its simple yet compelling good vs. evil premise, jettisoning some past characters and subplots while ensuring the ones remaining all align with the same goal: you exist to either defeat Sauron or to serve him."

Rings of Power Season 3 Episodes 1–4 is available to stream on Prime Video now . Episodes 5 and 6 premiere November 18, and Episodes 7 and 8 come out November 25.

articles.title: New Mega Man Legends Game, Movie, or TV Series Possibly In the Works After Fans Spot 'New Media' Listing
articles.summary: A now-deleted listing for ‘Mega Man Legends — New Media’ was spotted on a ‘What’s Shooting’ page for ACTRA Toronto, hinting that a new game, film, or TV series in the franchise's 'Legends' series is in the works.
articles.body:
A now-deleted listing for ‘Mega Man Legends — New Media’ was spotted on a ‘What’s Shooting’ page for ACTRA Toronto, hinting that a new game, film, or TV series in the franchise's 'Legends' series is in the works.

Although it’s since been deleted, several publications were able to screenshot the listing before it was taken down. The project’s start date was listed as September 14, 2026, with an end date of December 1, 2026. Casting was listed as “in-house.”

ACTRA Toronto’s What’s Shooting page is a public database that compiles ongoing projects that are registered with Canada’s performers’ union, the Alliance of Canadian Cinema, Television and Radio Artists. The Mega Man project’s ‘New Media’ label is especially intriguing, as this doesn’t necessarily denote that a new game is being made; rather, it’s vague enough to encompass any manner of projects, including movies or TV shows.

A Mega Man Legends movie isn’t out of the question, especially given Capcom’s recent foray into the world of Hollywood films. Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil adaptation was wildly successful, and hopes are high for a sequel to Legendary’s Street Fighter flick. In fact, Capcom has been working toward a screen adaptation of Mega Man for some time; the developer confirmed that a movie was being made in 2018 , which was initially being handled by 20th Century Fox (now 20th Century Studios).

Things were quiet for the next few years until 2020, when Henry Joost and Ariel Schulman, who were set to write and direct this movie, confirmed that it was still very much in production .

“We are super excited about it. I think we’re going to have some big news about it soon. I can’t say all that much right now, but it’s a project very near and dear to our hearts and we’re psyched,” Joost said at the time.

Mega Man: Dual Override – TGS 2026 Proto Man Screenshots

In 2021, Netflix announced that it was making a live action film based on Capcom’s legacy 2D platformer, which appeared to be unrelated to 20th Century’s Mega Man project. For now, it’s unclear if this newest listing is involved with either of those productions, and the slim information that's been provided is making fans' imaginations run wild.

Of course, most players are keen for a Mega Man Legends remake, or at least another title in that particular series. The first Mega Man Legends game was released all the way back in 1998; a sequel came out in 2000, and a spin-off title, The Misadventures of Tron Bonne , launched in 1999. With Dual Override coming in 2027, and Capcom expressing an interest in reviving its older IP , it’s certainly possible that there’s already another Mega Man title in the works — and remakes of legacy games are proving to be a real hit right now, after all.

For now, Mega Man fans can check out our interview with Dual Override’s Director Shinya Ikuta, Producer Hiroyuki Minamitani, Art Director Yuji Ishihara, and Art Director Shinsuke Komaki, where we asked them all about the game and what players can expect when it finally releases.

articles.title: Henry Cavill Is Open to Returning as Superman Once Again
articles.summary: Henry Cavill has stated that he's still open to the idea of playing Superman following all the shake-ups at DC Studios.
articles.body:
Henry Cavill has stated that he's still open to the idea of playing Superman following all the shake-ups at DC Studios.

In an interview with Inverse , Cavill was asked if he'd ever be interested in playing Superman again, and the interviewer suggested the Kingdom Come storyline as a possibility. Cavill noted he would never say never to the idea, and that there are a lot of "fantastic storylines" to adapt for Superman.

"Look, there's lots of fantastic storylines. There's always a lot of opportunity. As the pigeon sang to Fievel in An American Tail, 'never say never.' And I buy into that. I’ve had such a wonderful time playing Superman in the past. I would never say never now."

Of course, the timing of these comments could not come at a more interesting moment. If this happened a week ago, no one would've thought much of it. However, earlier this week, DC Studios heads James Gunn and Peter Safran were ousted from the company . They remain on board until December 1, when a new head, Jeremy Latcham, will take over. Latcham is expected to make changes to DC's direction, possibly resulting in a reboot, though that has yet to be firmly decided. His ultimate vision, however, is to focus on DC's mainstream characters in an effort to quickly assemble the Justice League on the big screen .

Presumably, they'll wait until James Gunn's Superman sequel, Man of Tomorrow, hits theaters in July to make a decision on whether they'll reboot or recast this DC universe. Cavill has famously been through a lot as Superman. His debut film, Man of Steel, was controversial thanks to the absurd casualties in his fight with General Zod. Batman v Superman also caused some friction with fans for a variety of reasons, one of which was that Superman was extremely brooding and miserable.

After the catastrophic disaster that was Justice League, Cavill's role as Superman remained in question. There were rumors he would be replaced, while others indicated the powers that be simply weren't sure what to do with him. Eventually, Dwayne 'The Rock' Johnson went above all of the WB execs and brought the actor back for a cameo in 2022's Black Adam, five years after Cavill's last appearance in the role. He was promised new Superman adventures ... but then, James Gunn took over DC just weeks later, and Cavill was essentially let go from the role .

The fact that Cavill is open to taking another crack at things after all of that is certainly interesting. Whether that opportunity ever comes remains to be seen, but it seems hard to imagine the new leadership reviving the Snyderverse.

articles.title: Nvidia Board Is Preparing to Potentially Oust CEO Jensen Huang
articles.summary: Three days after launching an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang, the Nvidia board is reportedly preparing to oust the executive.
articles.body:
Three days after launching an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang , the Nvidia board is reportedly preparing to oust the executive.

Nvidia's board will be meeting as soon as today to discuss Huang's future after an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese spy, according to The Wall Street Journal. That affair was first reported by The New York Times and was followed up by a statement issued by Nvidia on Sunday , saying it'd be investigating its CEO. According to a new report from The New York Times , he'd also engaged in a second affair with an executive who reported to him.

This meeting follows an investigation that was announced on Sunday. In that announcement, Nvidia said, "The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of Nvidia and its shareholders. While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information. Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it."

Huang then issued a letter to employees, obtained by the BBC , where he admitted that he was unfaithful and apologized for hurting his wife and children.

In many ways, Jensen Huang is the face of AI in the U.S., and so it makes sense that Nvidia's board would want to get this situation under control. The company's chips power nearly every AI model that's currently running, and so a security breach of this scale is a massive liability. Huang is a co-founder of Nvidia and has been running the company since 1993, so his ousting could have huge ramifications.

IGN has reached out to Nvidia for comment and will update this story as soon as communications have been received.

articles.title: AMC App Experiences Slowdown As Marvel Fans Rush to Buy Doomsday Tickets After VisionQuest Finale
articles.summary: So many Marvel fans tried to snag their tickets for Avengers: Doomsday after watching the VisionQuest season finale that they literally crashed the AMC Theaters app.
articles.body:
So many Marvel fans tried to snag their tickets for Avengers: Doomsday after watching the VisionQuest season finale that they literally crashed the AMC Theatres app. At least, that's what users are saying.

The crash reportedly occurred on the night of November 10 — the same night that the VisionQuest finale aired, which included a post-credits scene that all but confirmed a particular character will show up in Avengers: Doomsday .

Shortly after the episode aired on Disney+, fans and Marvel fanpages shared that the AMC app was showing an error message when they tried to use it, which asked them to “please try again.” They were unable to navigate to other pages within the app; it seems that it was totally unusable during this time.

Of course, viewers instantly pointed to the VisionQuest season finale as the reason for this, indicating that the hype levels were high enough to warrant a mass of fan interest in seeing Doomsday in theaters.

In a statement to IGN, an AMC Theatres spokesperson revealed that there was a 30-minute period where "some transactions were taking longer than normal." The spokesperson said that the AMC app didn't outright crash, as data showed that tickets continued to get sold throughout this period, but indicated that some users may have run into that error message during that time.

Warning : Major spoilers for VisionQuest below!

It’s no surprise that Marvel fans got so excited about Doomsday after this. The finale’s post-credits scene, which was also kept a secret from the media, showed Wanda Maximoff, aka the Scarlet Witch, having an interaction with Doctor Doom.

The specific scene returns to the ending of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness, in which the Scarlet Witch sacrifices herself by destroying the Darkhold. While viewers were under the impression that her heroic decision ultimately lead to her death, this isn’t the case. Doctor Doom appears and frees her from the rubble that had collapsed on top of her, saying, "Scarlet Witch, awaken. Your power will be mine." She comes to with a shocked expression before the scene ends.

Given that the Scarlet Witch has been officially confirmed to be alive after four years of ambiguity, fans are understandably beside themselves with excitement. On social media, viewers wasted no time sharing their hype for the scene in response to AMC’s app crash, with one writing , “That’s the Scarlet Witch effect!”

“Wanda impact,” another wrote , while another said the crash happened “all because of Wanda Maximoff!”

“Mother is that powerful,” another superfan said . “We’re ready to support anything she does because she can do no wrong.”

Avengers: Doomsday releases in theaters on December 18, 2026. While you’re waiting, you can watch Avengers: Endgame Encore , which has been re-released with new scenes and will be available to stream on Disney+ this Friday.

articles.title: From the Ashes Walkthrough - Crimson Desert Guide - IGN
articles.summary: From the Ashes is the second main story quest in the Charting the Unknown DLC for Crimson Desert. Damiane finds herself in the middle of a chaotic Demeniss,
articles.body:
From the Ashes is the second main story quest in the Charting the Unknown DLC for Crimson Desert . Damiane finds herself in the middle of a chaotic Demeniss, filled with unhappy protesters. Track down Countess Azerian to see how you can calm down the streets to deal with the unrest. This IGN guide covers how to complete all nine subquests within From the Ashes. Click the links below to jump straight to our dedicated walkthroughs:

After finishing the original main questline and completing Epilogue: Journey's End , this new quest becomes available. While playing as Damiane, return to Demeniss and make your way past the castle to the eastern side of town . You'll find a group of protesters not far from where Countess Azerian is.

Speak to the countess to discuss the unrest plaguing the city. As the protesters, politicians, and nobles speak, it's clear they're not happy with how things currently are. The countess chats on about how the streets still need time to heal. Which is quickly clear as rocks are thrown and even Antumbra Followers are preaching about the darkness.

As the countess leaves due to the city becoming dangerous, Damiane sets out to make it safe again. Before the cutscene here ends, Kliff appears and offers to help as well. Once the cutscene is over, you'll have three locations to visit to quell the chaos in Demeniss. We've included a small section for each one below.

One spot for this objective is near the Demeniss bank , a little east of the center of the quest zone. Just outside the bank, you'll find a group of thugs down an alley, harassing a stranger. Approach them to start a cutscene and fight. During this battle, you won't have access to your weapons, so you'll need to rely on your punches and kicks.

Once you've finished dealing with the thugs, the two strangers will thank you for your help.

The second spot is a little farther east from the previous one in this guide. You'll find two strangers down an alley, at a dead end. One is leaning over the other, who is injured on the ground. Head over to them to start a cutscene where they beg you to carry him to a healer.

After the cutscene ends, interact with the man on the ground to start carrying them . You can then run southeast to the quest objective. It'll take you beyond one gate toward the outer walls, where a cloth canopy is along the road.

Help the Novice Who is Running Out of Room For Patients

The third spot is conveniently next to the previous one. After carrying the injured man to the relief station, you'll find a larger tent to the south. Speak to the Novice lady waiting outside the tent. She'll explain that she's running out of room for incoming patients. This is where Damiane offers to try and figure something out for her.

This objective can be a little confusing if you're not sure of what to do or where to look. First, look for a table a little out from the front of the tent. It'll have a mallet and several massive stakes on it. Grab the mallet and equip it via your radial menu from the tool slot. Then, pick up a stake and carry it toward the tent. You'll find one stake spot on the right side and one on the left side.

If you're having trouble finding the stake spot, you can use your lantern to reveal an exclamation point above each one. Once you've placed the stake down, hammer it in with your mallet. As you may know from earlier in Crimson Desert, make sure the circle is blue while aiming your mallet to smack it into the ground.

After hammering in two stakes, check the other quest area on your minimap. You'll find a wagon there with a few Relief Supplies crates near it. Carry them over to the wagon and place them inside. After dropping three into it, push the back of the wagon forward toward the stall ahead.

This leads to a cutscene of the Novice thanking you for your efforts. Which then transitions into another cutscene showing Damiane checking in on more people to help. After doing as much as she can, she decides to speak with the countess again for help. This completes the Reclaimed and Remaining subquest.

Make your way over to the Azerian Manor , a little west of the town of Demeniss. This places it a tiny bit north of Easelbury. Once you arrive, head upstairs to trigger a cutscene almost immediately. Damiane starts looking for the countess, but after not finding her, a servant suddenly appears.

The worried servant explains that the countess left urgently and still hasn't returned. This leads to Damiane asking him to gather the guards as she embarks on her own search to track the countess down. Once the cutscene is over, Demeniss in Upheaval is complete.

articles.title: The 2026 LEGO Star Wars Advent Calendar Is Discounted at Target After Amazon Sells Out
articles.body:
This year's lineup of LEGO Advent Calendars have started going out of stock ahead of Black Friday . Unsurprisingly, the Star Wars-themed calendar is one of the first to have completely disappeared from major retailers. articles.title: Constantine Director 'Hopeful' for Sequel After DC Studios Shakeup
articles.summary: The director of Constantine, Francis Lawrence, opened up about the movie's long-awaited sequel now that DC Studios has had a changing of the guard.
articles.body:
The director of Constantine, Francis Lawrence, opened up about the movie's long-awaited sequel now that DC Studios has had a changing of the guard.

James Gunn and Peter Safran are out at DC Studios in a sudden and unexpected move that has sparked no end of worry and speculation among fans. Gunn, for his part, cited a distaste for the “corporate” side of the job, but confirmed that projects already in motion, like Man of Tomorrow , are still a-go.

Fans aren’t the only ones scratching their heads about what might happen next. Francis Lawrence, the director of oodles of Hollywood blockbusters, is also in this boat — though he’s rather optimistic about the situation, as it means he might finally get the chance to make another Constantine film.

Speaking with Collider ahead of his next movie, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping , Lawrence clarified that he isn’t happy for anyone to lose their jobs, but admitted that he’s keen on the possibility of getting Constantine 2 off the ground now that things are changing at DC.

"Well, I’ll tell you this,” he began. “Not that I want anybody to lose their jobs, so this is not like a schadenfreude kind of thing, but I will say that we’ve been trying to make Constantine 2 for twenty-something years, and we have an idea, and we have a script, and we’ve been wanting to make it, and the people that were at DC were an impediment to us making it.

“So, we are now more hopeful as of yesterday’s news that maybe now there will be another opportunity. But again, we’ve been trying to make this for twenty-something years, and there’s always been obstacles in the road to making it, and it’s not me, it’s not Keanu, it’s not Akiva. J.J. [Abrams] is on it, as well. We all want to do it. So, it’s really going to be people at Paramount, Warner, whoever’s running DC now, getting everybody on board to say, like, 'Hey, we can do a sequel of our version of Constantine?'"

Lawrence said, without a doubt, that this version of Constantine will be another R-Rated film, no matter what. He explained that the first movie had been made with a PG-13 rating in mind, but despite their best efforts, it was hit with an R label. If given the chance to make a sequel, Lawrence wants to lean all-in and make it a true R-rated experience.

“So, part of the idea from the very beginning was, because we followed all the rules to make a PG-13 movie and we got hit with an R, they told us, 'You can’t do anything about it. It’s going to be an R no matter what.' We tried to fight them on it, and they said, 'Nope. It’s an R,' but really, it’s an R-rated PG-13 movie, which pisses me off,” he explained.

"And so we all kind of came back and said, 'Okay, when we do this next time, we’re making the hard-R version of Constantine.' So when we do it, it’s going to be the hard-R version of Constantine."

Lawrence doubled down on his desire to make another Constantine at all costs, even saying that he doesn’t mind if it gets put into a shared universe or remade to fit DC’s ever-evolving plans at some point. He claimed that he and Keanu would even compromise on their financial compensation to get the film made, if that's what it takes.

"Personally, I don’t even care if somebody has a plan for some sort of shared universe, and they want to do another version of Constantine. If they just let us do the sequel to our version, they can coexist. So, I have renewed hope as of yesterday that there might be some possibility for forward movement there,” he said.

"We have to be responsible,” he continued, speaking about the financial side of the equation. “We want to make it. This is not the kind of movie that I would charge full freight and Keanu could charge full freight. It’s something we have to do, because we love and want to take a gamble on it, and do it responsibly. And so, we’ve been thinking about that same idea for 20 years, that we’re not going to do it for $100 million. We have to be scrappy about it."

Constantine was released in 2005. Starring Keanu Reeves, the movie is based on the DC/Vertigo comic book Hellblazer and follows supernatural detective John Constantine in his mission to purge the world of nefarious evil entities.

This is the latest news about Constantine after Reeves reportedly pitched a sequel to DC Studios in 2025. And just earlier this month, it was revealed that Evil Dead Wrath writer-director Francis Galluppi was hired by DC Studios to write a John Constantine movie for them, though it’s unclear if he’ll also be directing.

articles.summary: Skullkid Ocarina Recital is a Mini-Game found in the Lost Woods in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. This mini-game requires you to memorize and
articles.body:
Skullkid Ocarina Recital is a Mini-Game found in the Lost Woods in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. This mini-game requires you to memorize and recite a randomly generated Ocarina song that gets longer as the game goes.

Check out IGN's full guide to Skullkid Ocarina Recital below.

Ocarina Recital is a mini-game that can be found in the Lost Woods. Go right from the Lost Woods entrance, then jump down into the grove straight ahead where you will see two Skull Kids playing instruments on large tree trunks. Stand on the stump and pull out your Ocarina and they'll start a game of "follow the tune". You'll need to repeat a randomized set of notes that build from 3-5, and if you can follow along, they'll pass you a Blue Rupee.

Try it again, and this time you'll have to follow the notes that build from 4-6. If you're having trouble as they hide which notes you need to memorize, look for the placement on the prompt to clue you in on which notes you need to remember. Complete this task, and you'll earn a Red Rupee worth 20.

Play their game one last time for a super hard version of following notes that build from 6 to 8. If you can keep following along, you'll earn the ultimate prize: a new Piece of Heart!

Bombchu Bowling is a mini-game located in Castle Town. You can find the Bombchu Bowling mini-game by entering the building to the west of the fountain. This mini-game only becomes available after getting the Bombs and completing Dodongo's Cavern.

Bombchu Bowling costs 10 Rupees to play. You get 10 Bombchus and need to destroy three increasingly difficult targets. You must hit the bright yellow spot to proceed. At first the target is usually straight ahead, but sometimes it appears along the side or in a corner. For these you will need to throw at an angle, so adjust carefully between throws and do not waste and Bombchus.

Diving Lesson is a Mini-Game found in the Zora Domain in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. This mini-game requires you to dive to collect silver scales strewn around the large pool in the Domain.

Diving Lesson is a mini-game in Zora Domain, found in the tunnel connected to King Zora’s room. Speak to the diving instructor to begin.

He will throw 5 scales into the water below the waterfall, and you need to dive down and collect them. The first go around you have plenty of time, so just position yourself above each scale then dive down to grab each one. Winning this mini-game gets you the Silver Scale.

Horse Racing is a one time mini-game at Lon Lon Ranch, as Adult Link only. Pay Ingo 20 Rupees to ride horses, then once inside play Epona’s Song to mount Epona.

Speak to Ingo while riding Epona and he will challenge you to a race. Beat Ingo in the horse race, then beat him again in a rematch to win Epona permanently (escape the Ranch by jumping over the outer gate).

articles.title: Interlude of Dreams Event Guide - Hello Kitty Island Adventure Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Interlude of Dreams is an Annual Event that begins on November 4 and will continue through the month as the sole event in Hello Kitty Island Adventure. The
articles.body:
Interlude of Dreams is an Annual Event that begins on November 4 and will continue through the month as the sole event in Hello Kitty Island Adventure . The theme this season is racing season! Participate by testing your driving skills at the new mini-game and earn Gears to unlock exclusive event outfits, furniture, and more!

How to Get Event Items and Rewards Formula Fun Mini-Game Rewards

Exclusive Flower and How to Grow Bowblossoms

Check in with Hello Kitty Island Adventure every day to get Daily Rewards from My Melody , or receive the items from the game menu by selecting the Daily Rewards icon to check in. These rewards feature exclusive outfits, Game Tickets, and resources that can be found around Friendship Island.

Interlude of Dreams’ Daily Rewards is broken down into three parts: Part I will last for 14 days and begin on the same day as the event; Part II will last for 10 days and begin a few days after the event has started. Interlude of Dreams' Finale will last 8 days and begin about a week after the event has started.

Interlude of Dreams 2026’s theme revolves around sports car racing ! Everyone has donned Raceway or Crew Pit Outfits to fit the theme, and an Award Podium has been set up shop in the park south of Seaside Resort's center plaza. Here you can exchange the Event Currency, Gears , for exclusive Raceway Furniture as well as outfits and furniture from previous Interlude of Dreams events.

In order to obtain Gears, you’ll need to participate in the Mini-Game that has been set up across from the Awards Podium. Formula Fun is a racing game where you’ll compete against your friends for 1st place. Pick a driver and a course to get started. Each race will cost 1x Game Ticket to play; you can obtain Game Tickets by collecting them from around Seaside Resort or logging in for Daily Rewards to obtain some extras for free.

Each race will last for 3 laps, and you’ll be racing against 5 other Hello Kitty drivers. Use the [ZR] and [ZL] buttons or the Right and Left Arrow Keys to control where your driver is on the road. You’ll have 3 Booster Charges that allow you to go faster for a short period of time, but these charges do not refill, so use them sparingly throughout the race.

The best way to win these races is by remaining close to the turns, sticking close to the red and white barriers , and using the Charges throughout the race to maintain a high speed to break away from the other racers. The best time to use these charges is during each lap when the racer has reached the long stretch of road that leads up to the goal. Maintain the turns, and then achieve a high speed down the straight road to max out your speed and take home the 1st prize every time.

By challenging Formula Fun daily, you’ll be rewarded with exclusive items from the Raceway theme, either outfits or furniture, as well as 10x Gears . If you happened to have missed a day, you can still make up for the Gears lost by not logging in for that day. When you miss up to a maximum of 3 days, you can play Formula Fun and receive 30x Gears . Placement does not matter when obtaining Gears; you’ll receive the same 10x daily even if you place last.

When completing the Formula Fun mini-game, you won't only be rewarded with Gears for the Interlude of Dreams event. By continuing to play the game and race against the Hello Kitty characters , you can win exclusive Raceway outfits and sports cars owned by the other Hello Kitty racers! Below are all of the items that you can receive upon completing the Formula Fun mini-game.

During the Interlude of Dreams, you may discover a new type of fauna in your empty Garden Plots around Friendship Island. These Flowers are known as Bowblossoms , a special flower that only grows around this time of year. Inspired by Hello Kitty's bow, the Bowblossom can spawn in three different colors naturally: Warm Pink , Lilac , and Seafoam .

By growing these flowers around Friendship Island and Merry Meadows , you can gain access to new pastel colors that you may not have had before and begin attempting to transfer those colors by planting them next to another flower of your choosing

Note that once the Interlude of Dreams event is over, you will not be able to grow new Bowblossoms in Seaside Resort or Merry Meadows. You can pick up these flowers once they are fully grown to take back to the Greenhouse in Merry Meadows to continue color transferring or attempting to unlock new pattern variations.

Event Flowers, like the Bowblossom, cannot be turned into Seed Packets . The best way to transfer them is by using a Trowel and only picking them up once they have grown past the sprout phase and have bloomed at least once.

Below are all of the map locations where you can find Bubble Trails in Seaside Resort. Run through these Bubbles to obtain them and use them for fun recipes and special treats!

During the Interlude of Dreams event, you may occasionally find Bubbles arranged in a pattern. By running through these, you can collect Bubbles and use them at various Appliances to unlock a new recipe! Below are all the recipes you can unlock with Bubbles and the Cooking Station you’ll need to craft them.

articles.title: Center Stage Walkthrough - Hello Kitty Island Adventure Guide - IGN
articles.summary: ”Center Stage” is one of the Special Gathering Quests for Retsuko’s Birthday on November 6 in Hello Kitty Island Adventure. Help Tuxedosam
articles.body:
”Center Stage” is one of the Special Gathering Quests for Retsuko’s Birthday on November 6 in Hello Kitty Island Adventure . Help Tuxedosam to arrange a birthday party for your favorite musician on the island. By completing this quest, you’ll be rewarded with a Retsuko Party Favor and Retsuko’s Birthday Balloons Crafting Plans .

Retsuko’s Birthday Quest will be available for some time before and after her actual birthday, starting initially on November 4 and ending on November 10 . If you have already completed “Center Stage”, then it will not appear again, but during this week, you’ll still be able to pick up Retsuko’s Decorating Kits .

Retsuko’s Decorating Kits can occasionally be found when picking up select items around Mount Hothead , such as Magma Blooms and Toasted Almonds . You can use Retsuko’s Decorating Kits at the Oven to bake Retsuko her very own birthday cake, decorated in her image!

To start the quest, talk to Tuxedosam in Seaside Resort . You’ll immediately be taken to his shop, where you happen to run into Retsuko. She mentions that she’s spending some time in the resort and walking along the beach to try and do something memorable for her birthday.

As Retsuko leaves the shop, Tuxedosam turns to you with a plan. Naturally, you have to arrange a party for Retsuko so that she can celebrate her birthday properly among friends. A quiet ball is more Tuxedosam’s style, but something karaoke- or music-themed should fit Retsuko’s aesthetics.

Tuxedosam suggests the Comedy Club for the venue and asks that you start prepping the drinks and snacks for the party. For that, you’ll need to borrow a couple of appliances, so head to the cafe to talk to Hello Kitty .

Of course, Hello Kitty is on board for baking for Retsuko’s birthday party and declares that there should be a variety for everyone coming to visit. To start, you’ll need to bake 5x Strawberry Shortcakes , 5x Cinnamon Bread , and 5x Pineapple Stack Cake .

Strawberry Shortcake Recipe: 1x Flour ( My Melody’s Daily Gift) and 1x Strawberry ( Pochacco’s Daily Gift)

Cinnamon Bread Recipe: 1x Flour (My Melody’s Daily Gift) and 1x Cinna Bloom/Magma Bloom ( Mount Hothead )

Pineapple Stack Cake Recipe: 1x Flour (My Melody’s Daily Gift) and 1x Pineapple (Seaside Resort)

Once everything has been baked, talk to Hello Kitty again. With all the snacks made, next come the drinks. For that, head to Gemstone Mountain to talk to Pekkle . Fast travel to the Gemstone Town Mailbox and talk to Pekkle nearby.

Like Hello Kitty, he thinks that the party should have some variety, so he suggests making 3x Cream Soda , 3x Sweet Soda , and 3x Fiery Soda .

Cream Soda Recipe: 1x Fizzy Crystal (Crafted from Fizzy Ore, found in Gemstone Mines) and 1x Coral Milk ( Rainbow Reef )

Sweet Soda Recipe: 1x Fizzy Crystal (Crafted from Fizzy Ore, found in Gemstone Mines) and 1x Candy Cloud ( Cinnamoroll’s Daily Gift) or 1x Swampmallow ( Spooky Swamp ) or 1x Sugarkelp ( Keroppi’s Daily Gift)

Fiery Soda Recipe: 1x Fizzy Crystal (Crafted from Fizzy Ore, found in Gemstone Mines) and 1x Toasted Almond (Mount Hothead) or 1x Cinna Bloom (Mount Hothead) or 1x Magma Bloom (Mount Hothead)

Talk to Pekkle once you’ve brewed all the drinks. Satisfied, he asks if there’s anything left on the list. All that remains now is gathering everyone and heading to the Comedy Club to set up Retsuko’s birthday party!

Once you’ve dived into Rainbow Reef, talk to Tuxedosam in the Comedy Club. He’s already begun some setup while you were getting the snacks and is joined by Hello Kitty, Badtz-maru , and Hangyodon . Everything looks ready, but Tuxedosam suggests that there is still something missing.

Retsuko is known for her spectacular singing and love of metal music. Tuxedosam hands you some balloons that were made in her image to decorate around the stage and bring the party’s aesthetics together.

Once properly decorated, talk to Hello Kitty for the group’s final appraisal. Tuxedosam is satisfied, but Badtz-maru thinks that there is still something missing. He was going to save the final surprise for a prank, but thinks it’ll suit the party better. Tuxedosam is concerned, doubly so when Badtz-maru has to make sure everyone clears out from the stage.

With everyone a safe distance away, Badtz-maru triggers some pyrotechnics on the stage! Tuxedosam is stunned and delighted, assured that this was indeed the perfect addition to the birthday party. Thanks to Hangyodon, the final-final step has already been arranged: inviting all the guests!

Retsuko shows up to witness a spectacular setup for her birthday, surrounded by all her friends with plenty of well wishes for her special day! With some time on karaoke, she thanks everyone for going through the trouble of arranging a party.

With the quest complete, Tuxedosam is gracious enough to share in the extra items he crafted, gifting you a Retsuko Party Favor and Retsuko’s Birthday Balloons Crafting Plans .

articles.title: Elon Musk Extends Cybertruck Production to 'Work Through' Order Backlog, Says There Must Be Room for 'Sentimentality'
articles.summary: Elon Musk has extended production of Cybertruck to work through an order backlog, the Tesla owner has said.
articles.body:
Elon Musk has extended production of Cybertruck to work through an order backlog, the Tesla owner has said.

Last week, the tech billionaire confirmed plans to wind down production of the Cybertruck at Tesla's gigafactory in Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production. Cybertruck lead engineer Wes Morrill then suggested that Cybertruck was being discontinued.

But Musk said today that production will now be extended through the end of summer 2027. He did not put a firm date on the end of production, but did provide some commentary around the decision, saying: “This is not the smartest move from a profit-maximizing standpoint btw, but there must be some room in this world for sentimentality or what’s the point?”

Tesla Cybertruck Official Release - Slideshow

The angular Cybertruck launched in 2023 to much fanfare, but sales have been poor. Indeed, the truck has suffered online ridicule ever since it was introduced in 2019, when Musk himself shattered its supposed unbreakable glass during a live demo.

While fans of both Musk and Cybertruck have welcomed the news, there is no suggestion here that Tesla is making a long-term commitment to production of the vehicle. The focus, now, is on Cybercab , which Musk has said will play a crucial role in Tesla’s robotaxi plans. According to Reuters , the two-seater robotaxi is still a small program, with production beginning only earlier this year. Tesla has listed an installed capacity of more than 125,000 units.
